info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package agents is autonomous agents for your org: define them, run them, keep every run.

get.summary: Returns every agent defined in the caller's org, each with the number of runs recorded against it.
get.description:
Returns every agent defined in the caller's org, each with the
number of runs recorded against it. A retired built-in is left out.

post.summary: Defines an agent in the caller's org: a model, a system prompt (instructions) and a set of tool names.
post.description:
Defines an agent in the caller's org: a model, a system prompt
(instructions) and a set of tool names. The name must be unique in the org and
match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. An omitted model takes the
deployment's configured default; a named one is checked against the gateway's
served catalog, so a model this deployment never serves is refused here rather
than failing at run time. A long-running agent must carry a 5-field cron
schedule (the scheduler would otherwise never fire it) and counts against a
per-org cap on scheduled agents. An agent spawned by another names it as its
parent; the parent must be an agent of the caller's org, and the new agent
carries its whole lineage.

post.summary: Talk to the Hanzo assistant over A2A (Agent2Agent 1.0, JSON-RPC).
post.description:
The A2A server its agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json names. Each SendMessage is a task the default assistant answers with the tools your credential reaches: an agent run like POST /v1/agent/:ref/run, so your balance is authorized before any inference and the flat run fee is charged only when the run succeeds. A request waits for the answer unless configuration.returnImmediately is set; either way the task is kept, and GetTask, ListTasks and CancelTask read and stop your own tasks. A conversation continues by sending the next message with the task's contextId.

Methods: SendMessage, GetTask, ListTasks, CancelTask. Streaming and push notifications answer UnsupportedOperation (-32004) and PushNotificationNotSupported (-32003). The A2A-Version header, when sent, is 1.0. With no credential the answer is 401 with a WWW-Authenticate challenge naming the protected-resource metadata; every other outcome, refusals included, is a JSON-RPC response.

get.summary: Serves the recent-activity feed.
get.description:
Serves the recent-activity feed. Events are REAL: each of the
caller's own recorded runs is an invoked (ok) or failed (error) event; each of
the org's agents' create/update timestamps are created/updated events. Merged, newest first,
capped. Nothing is invented — an org with no agents and no runs gets [].

post.summary: The MCP server a coding run's harness asks its person through.
post.description:
Speaks MCP over streamable HTTP and serves one tool, ask_user: a question and 2 to 8 options, shown as buttons in the run's thread, answered by the person the run is for. The call waits for the answer, up to 30 minutes, streaming as text/event-stream with a comment every 15 seconds, and returns it as the tool's result, or says none came.

The caller is a coding run, not a tenant: the request carries the run's ticket in X-Hanzo-Run and no bearer. The ticket is minted for one run, opens this server and nothing else, names the run the question belongs to, and ends with the run. A request without a live ticket is 401, and any tool but ask_user is refused.

post.summary: Run one tool-calling round against your org's own tools
post.description:
Answers one turn of a conversation with four things: the model's `reply`, the `actions` the server executed on the caller's behalf, the `ops` the client must apply itself, and the `conversationId` the turn was recorded under.

The split between actions and ops is the rule most easily got wrong. A tool call is executed HERE only when the chosen preset is server-executing AND the tool resolves in the caller's own scope; every other call is handed back as an op for the client to apply to its own graph or UI. A tool that fails still comes back as an action, carrying its error rather than failing the round.

`preset` selects the system prompt and the tool set (`capability` is a legacy alias for it); an unknown one is refused. `conversationId` continues an existing thread, and its absence starts one. A validated principal with a non-empty org is required — the org is the sole authority for both persistence and tool scope, and is NEVER read from the body.

A completion refused for the caller's own reason — 402 insufficient balance, 429, 403 — is relayed with its own status and body verbatim, so the real billing message reaches the client instead of an opaque gateway error. Only a genuine upstream fault becomes a 502.

get.summary: List your own conversations
get.description:
Returns a summary of each conversation the caller opened — id, title, when it was last appended to, and whether it is pinned or archived — for populating a thread list: pinned first, then most recent. Archived conversations are left out; `?archived=true` lists them alone.

A conversation is the person's who opened it, not the org's: another member of the same org lists none of it. Each org's conversations live in a store of its own, and inside it only the caller's are listed. One recorded before members were kept names nobody and is nobody's: `?memberless=true` lists those instead, for a SuperAdmin alone (403 for anyone else), and each such list is audited. A validated principal naming an org and a user the identity boundary attests no two people share is required: 401 without a principal, 403 without an org or such a user.

post.summary: Record turns in a conversation
post.description:
Writes turns to the caller's thread store without running a completion, and answers the `conversationId` they were written under. An absent `conversationId` opens a new thread; supplying one appends to it.

This is for a client that streams its own turn through /v1/chat/completions and still wants the conversation in its history — the round records what IT answers, and is otherwise the only writer. It takes the same store, the same per-org isolation and the same notion of a thread: what is recorded here reads back through the two GETs beside it and the round can continue it by id. A validated principal with a non-empty org is required: 401 without a principal, 403 without an org.

delete.description: Removes the conversation for good: every turn of it, and every link it was shared by, which stops opening and leaves the lists of the people it was open to. Only the member who opened it may delete it; anyone else is answered 404, as for one that is not there. Every delete is written to the audit trail.

get.summary: Read one agent thread in full
get.description:
Returns every message of one of the caller's conversations in order — role, content, the assistant's tool calls where it made any, and each message's creation time — which is the transcript a client replays to resume a thread.

Another member's conversation, another org's, and one recorded with no member are answered 404, exactly as an id that never existed, so an id says nothing about whose it is (a SuperAdmin alone reads one with no member, and each read is audited). A turn sent under such an id opens a fresh conversation of the caller's. A validated principal naming an org and a user is required: 401 without a principal, 403 without an org or a user.

patch.summary: Rename, pin or archive one of your conversations
patch.description:
Takes `{title?, pinned?, archived?}` and changes what it names, leaving the rest; a body naming none is refused 400, and so is an empty title. A title is cut to one line of at most 80 characters. Answers the conversation as the list does — id, title, updatedAt, pinned, archived — and the change does not move `updatedAt`, which stays when it was last spoken in.

The list puts pinned conversations first and leaves archived ones out; `?archived=true` lists those alone. Only the member who opened the conversation may change it; another member's, another org's, and one recorded with no member answer 404. Every change is written to the audit trail.

get.summary: List the live links to one of your conversations
get.description: Returns each unrevoked share of a conversation the caller owns: its id, its access (`read`), when it was made, and its `viewers` — each signed-in person who opened it, with the name they signed in with and when. Tokens are not in the list; they are returned only when a share is made.

post.summary: Share one of your conversations by link
post.description:
Makes a read-only link to a conversation the caller owns and answers the share and its `token`. The token is 256 random bits and is returned ONCE: the store keeps only its SHA-256, so a lost token is replaced by making another share, never read back. The token names the chat and authenticates nobody.

A share is a snapshot of the user and assistant turns up to the moment it was made. System turns, tool calls and tool results are never part of it, and turns added later need a new share. Only the member who opened the conversation may share it; anyone else — and anyone at all for a conversation recorded with no member — is answered 404. Every share made is written to the audit trail.

delete.summary: Revoke a link to one of your conversations
delete.description: Ends one share of a conversation the caller owns, for every viewer: it leaves their lists, and its token opens nothing and reads exactly like a token that never existed. Every revoke is written to the audit trail.

delete.summary: Remove one viewer from a link
delete.description: Closes one share of a conversation the caller owns to one viewer: it leaves their list, and the token no longer opens it for them. Everyone else the share is open to keeps it. Every removal is written to the audit trail.

get.summary: List the agent presets available to a caller
get.description:
Returns the preset catalog: each entry's id, its description and whether it is server-executing — the flag that decides if a preset's tool calls run here or come back for the client to apply. The ids are what the round accepts in `preset`.

The catalog is compiled into the build, identical for every caller, and this is the one read in the group that needs no principal.

get.summary: List the chats shared with you
get.description: Returns each live share the caller opened signed in: its id, the conversation's title and when the caller first opened it, most recent first. A revoked share, or one its owner closed to the caller, is not in it. A signed-in person is required.

get.summary: Read a chat shared with you
get.description: Returns the snapshot of a share the caller is a viewer of, without its token, in the shape POST /shares/read answers a signed-in person. Anyone who is not one of its viewers is answered 404.

get.summary: List every live link in your organization
get.description: For an admin of the caller's organization: every unrevoked share made in it, with the conversation's id and title, the member who made it, when, and how many people it is open to. `?user=` narrows it to one member's. Anyone else is answered 403, and so is an admin of a held org such as hanzo, whose members are customers who are strangers to each other.

post.summary: Open a conversation shared by link
post.description: Takes `{token}` in the body, so the token never sits in a URL a log keeps. A caller who is not a signed-in person gets the title and `full: false`, and no turn of the transcript — which is what a sign-in prompt shows. A signed-in person, of any org, is recorded as a viewer the owner can see, and reads the whole snapshot with the share's id; the reader's own org is neither read nor changed. An assistant turn carries `model` only when this server stored it from that model's completion. A token that does not open — malformed, unknown, revoked, or closed to this viewer — is answered 404 with one sentence for all.

delete.summary: Revoke any link in your organization
delete.description: For an admin of the caller's organization: ends one share made in it, for every viewer, exactly as its owner's revoke does. Anyone else is answered 403 (an admin of a held org included), and a share of another organization 404. Every revoke is written to the audit trail.

post.summary: Start one autonomous coding run against a repo in the caller's org
post.description:
Runs a coding task on a repository: clones it into a sandbox, lets a model read
and edit the code, run the tests, and push the work to a branch. Say the thing
you want done — "fix the failing auth test in hanzoai/cloud" — and the run
infers the repo, the branch and the plan. No prefix, no ceremony.

Name no repo and the run works in an empty workspace of its own: nothing is
cloned and nothing is pushed, and what it makes is kept in its sandbox and as
its artifacts. Name a repository the caller can read and not push to — a public
one — and it is cloned read-only, the same way.

It answers 202 with the run's handle the moment the run is ADMITTED — not when
it finishes. A coding run takes minutes; holding a request open for one would
tie a connection to a model loop and give the caller nothing it cannot get
better from the session stream.

The handle is a session id, and that is deliberate: the session is already the
run's durable record and its live stream (/v1/agent/sessions/stream?root=<id>), so
this op does not grow a progress endpoint, a status endpoint or a cancel
endpoint of its own. One way to watch a run, whoever started it.

It is also how work CONTINUES. Pass an earlier run's session as `after` and
this one starts from where that one stopped, so "now add tests for it" builds
on the branch already pushed instead of a fresh clone. The follow-up has its
own session and writes the same branch, so one piece of work is one branch and
one pull request however many instructions it takes.

Pass `branch` to name the branch the run writes (`agent/<name>`), and `pull`
as false to push it without opening a pull request.

Pass `requestId`, or the Idempotency-Key header, to make a retry the same
request: one run, whichever pod takes the retry and whatever restarts between,
and the retry answers the first's handle. The same id with another request is
422, and an id is at most 256 bytes.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this request the same request: one run for this
caller whichever pod takes the retry and whatever restarts between, and the
retry answers what the first answered. The Idempotency-Key header is the same
value, and wins when both are sent. Optional.

get.summary: Returns what a coding run changed, read from the forge it pushed its branch to: the commits on its branch that the base does not have, newest first; the net change of the branch against its base, one entry per file with that file's patch; and its pull request with the reviews it has had, or null while it has none.
get.description:
Returns what a coding run changed, read from the forge it pushed its branch
to: the commits on its branch that the base does not have, newest first; the
net change of the branch against its base, one entry per file with that file's
patch; and its pull request with the reviews it has had, or null while it has
none. `steers` lists the instructions said to the run while no pod held it, each
queued until the run took it and delivered after.

A run whose branch is not on the forge yet — still working, or finished with
nothing to change — answers with no commits, no files and no pull request.
Every read is made as the caller, so a repository they cannot open on the
forge is not found here either, whoever can see the run.

One answer is bounded, and says where it was cut rather than failing: the
newest 250 commits (`moreCommits` when there are more), the change up to 8 MiB
of diff or 3000 files (`moreFiles`, the last file marked truncated), and the
first 50 reviews (`moreReviews`), each body up to 16 KiB and 256 KiB across
them (`truncated` on a cut one). A caller has at most two of these reads in
flight and is answered 429 past that; two asking for the same change at once
share one read.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description:
Session is the run's handle — the sessionId POST /v1/agent/coding answered
with — from the path.

post.summary: Gives your running coding run more time.
post.description:
Gives your running coding run more time. A run is held to the time it was asked
for (`timeoutSeconds`) and, when it is up, keeps its work on its branch and
ends; this moves that time later while the run works, so a task expected to
take five minutes that is nearly done is given two more rather than restarted.
`seconds` is added to the time the run has left, as far as the longest a run
may be given; the answer says when the run is up now, so asking for more than
that reads what you got.

The run must be yours and still working: a run that is paused or already out
of time is a conflict (start a new one with `after` set to its session), and
one that is not running is not found. A run sent to a machine of your own
keeps that machine's time and cannot be extended.

`requestId`, or the Idempotency-Key header, makes a retry the same request: the
time is added once, and the retry answers what the first answered. The same id
with another request is 422.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Session is the run's handle, from the path.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this request the same request: the time is added
once, and the retry answers what the first answered. The Idempotency-Key
header is the same value, and wins when both are sent. Optional.

post.summary: Merges a coding run's pull request into the branch it proposes into, on the forge the run pushed to, and answers the pull request after.
post.description:
Merges a coding run's pull request into the branch it proposes into, on the
forge the run pushed to, and answers the pull request after.

The caller must be able to read the run: its person, or an admin of its org.
What lands is the run's branch at the commit the forge holds when this asks —
a push after that is refused, not merged unseen — and nothing is forced: a
pull request that conflicts, was closed, or that a rule on its base keeps
from merging is 409 with the forge's reason. One already merged answers as
it is. `requestId`, or the Idempotency-Key header, makes a retry the same
request, answered as the first was; the same id with another request is 422.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Session is the run's handle, from the path.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this merge the same merge, answered as the first
was. The Idempotency-Key header is the same value, and wins when both are sent.
Optional.

post.summary: Opens the pull request for the branch a coding run pushed, as the run's person and with no agent run, and answers its number and address.
post.description:
Opens the pull request for the branch a coding run pushed, as the run's person
and with no agent run, and answers its number and address.

A run pushes its branch and stops; the pull request is the step after, taken
when the work is ready. A run that already has an open pull request, or a
branch that has one on its host, answers with that one, so asking twice is
safe. Title, body, base and draft are optional: the title and body come from
the run's task, the base is the branch the run started from, and draft opens it
as one a reviewer cannot merge yet. The run's branch must be on its host: a run
that pushed nothing, or has not pushed yet, is 409. Who may is who may read the
run, and the pull request is read back at GET /v1/agent/coding/{session}/changes.
`requestId`, or the Idempotency-Key header, makes a retry the same request,
answered as the first was; the same id with another request is 422.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Session is the run's handle, from the path.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this request the same request, answered as the
first was. The Idempotency-Key header is the same value, and wins when both
are sent. Optional.

post.summary: Redirect your running or paused coding session.
post.description:
Redirect your running or paused coding session. On an active dev turn the
instruction is queued into the running turn in place; otherwise the current
run keeps its work before starting a follow-up. Ownership comes from the
authenticated credential, never the request body.

A run that no pod holds at that moment, between the halves of a rolling restart
or while it is resumed, keeps the instruction in its inbox and takes it, once and
in order, when its owner is up; GET /v1/agent/coding/{session}/changes lists these
as `steers`, queued or delivered, and the answer says `queued` while the run has
not taken the instruction. A run that has ended refuses it with 409. `requestId`,
or the Idempotency-Key header, makes a retry the same instruction: said once,
whichever pod takes the retry and whatever restarts between. The same id with
another instruction is 422.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Session identifies the running or paused coding session from the path.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this instruction the same instruction: said once to
the run, whichever pod takes the retry and whatever restarts between. The
Idempotency-Key header is the same value, and wins when both are sent.
Optional.

post.summary: The MCP address a coding run's harness reaches one of its org's MCP servers through.
post.description:
Speaks MCP over streamable HTTP for one of the org's MCP servers, named by its id: tools/list answers the tools of it an admin of the org activated, and tools/call calls one. The server's address and credential never reach the run: the tool plane adds the credential and dials the server.

The caller is a coding run, not a tenant: the request carries the run's ticket in X-Hanzo-Run and no bearer. A request without a live ticket is 401, and a server the run's kit did not carry when it started is 403. A run has at most four requests in flight here and twenty in a burst, then one a second; a request past that is 429 with Retry-After.

get.summary: Serves the invocations-over-time histogram for the Agents dashboard, over the caller's own runs.
get.description:
Serves the invocations-over-time histogram for the Agents
dashboard, over the caller's own runs. Every point is a REAL count of recorded
runs in that time bucket —
one series line per agent that ran in the window. The Resource Usage rollup is
all-null because this store meters no CPU/memory/storage/cost; the console
renders those as "—" rather than a fabricated figure. No runs => empty series
(an honest "not connected / no activity yet"), never a synthesized trend.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Range is the window to bucket: 24H, 7D or 30D. Anything else reads as 30D.

get.summary: Returns the caller's own agent runs across EVERY agent of the org, newest first — what ran, on which model, how long it took, and why it failed.
get.description:
Returns the caller's own agent runs across EVERY agent of the org,
newest first — what ran, on which model, how long it took, and why it failed.
A run is the person's who asked for it: another member's never appears, and a
run no person asked for (a schedule) appears to a SuperAdmin alone.

It is the feed the per-agent history could not be: an operator asking "what is
this tenant's agent plane doing" does not start out knowing an agent ref, and
answering by listing the agents and then paging each one's history is N+1 round
trips to reconstruct one ordering the database already has (RunsSince, ordered
by created_at over the org index).

The org is the CALLER's, resolved from identity by tenantStore — never a
parameter. There is deliberately no org field on orgRunsQuery to forge: run
history is the tenant's own record, and the only tenant this can answer for is
the one asking.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps how many runs come back, newest first. Absent, zero or out of
range (1..200) reads as 50.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status keeps only runs with this outcome ("ok" or "error"). Empty keeps
both. It is the filter an operator reaches for first — "show me what broke"
— and answering it here rather than by paging the whole history client-side
is the difference between a usable feed and a download.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's live sessions, newest first — each with its event count, its direct-child count and a one-line preview of its latest event.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's live sessions, newest first — each with
its event count, its direct-child count and a one-line preview of its latest
event. With no filter it returns ROOT sessions only, so a dashboard shows one
row per flow rather than one per subagent; ?root= or ?parent= descends.

parameters.name: root
parameters.description: Root scopes the page to one subagent tree (its root session id).

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description:
Parent scopes the page to the direct children of one session. Ignored when
root is set; with neither, only ROOT sessions come back.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Status filters to running, paused, done or error.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project filters to the sessions tagged with one product slug.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description:
Channel filters to the sessions started in one collaborative channel — the query a
space view runs to show what has been run in it.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
Kind filters to the sessions of one kind of run: "coding" lists coding runs,
each carrying its repo, base, branch, environment and pull request.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the page. Absent, zero or over 500 reads as 100.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: After is the `next` of the previous page. Absent starts at the newest.

post.summary: Opens a live agent session in the caller's org — the row every surface (the CLI's outer agent, hanzo.bot, the console, chat) hangs its activity off.
post.description:
Opens a live agent session in the caller's org — the row every
surface (the CLI's outer agent, hanzo.bot, the console, chat) hangs its
activity off. A session with a parentSessionId becomes a subagent of that
session and inherits its root, so one flow is one tree; without one it is
itself a root. Registering with a terminal status records a session that has
already finished.

get.summary: Live session and event updates for the caller's org, as Server-Sent Events.
get.description:
Holds the connection open as text/event-stream and pushes a frame each time the org's registry moves: an `event: session` frame carrying the same session shape the list and detail reads answer with (a registration, an update, or a login-manager revoke tearing a session down), and an `event: event` frame carrying one appended turn (with `id: <seq>`). Optional ?root=<session id> narrows the feed to a single subagent tree, and optional ?after=<seq> (or the `Last-Event-ID` request header) replays stored events with `seq > after` in order before streaming live updates without duplicates.

Requires a validated principal carrying an org: 401 without a principal, 403 without an org. Org-scoped fail-closed: the bus filters on tenant before it fans out, so a subscriber only ever receives its own org's updates, and ?root= narrows that further but can never widen it. Within the org a subscriber receives what GET /v1/agent/sessions/{id} would show them: a member the frames of the sessions they opened, an org admin or a SuperAdmin the org's.

Delivery is best-effort and the GET reads remain the source of truth. A subscriber that falls more than 256 frames behind is DROPPED — its channel is closed and the stream ends — so one stuck dashboard can never back-pressure a session write; the client reconnects and re-reads the session endpoints to resynchronise. A `: ping` comment every 25 seconds holds the connection open through proxies and is how a departed client is noticed.

delete.summary: Stops a session if it is still live, settles any unbilled runtime, and removes the session, its subagent subtree, and their recorded events from the caller org's registry.
delete.description:
Stops a session if it is still live, settles any unbilled
runtime, and removes the session, its subagent subtree, and their recorded
events from the caller org's registry.

Only the session's owner — or, in a customer org for non-private sessions, an
org admin or SuperAdmin — may delete it; another member's session, a
cross-tenant id, and an unknown id all answer 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to act on, from the path.

get.summary: Returns one session with its direct child sessions and a page of its events, oldest of those first (50 from the tail by default, up to `limit` up to 1000, or forward from `after` with a `next` cursor).
get.description:
Returns one session with its direct child sessions and a page of
its events, oldest of those first (50 from the tail by default, up to `limit`
up to 1000, or forward from `after` with a `next` cursor). The children are
those the caller may see, by the rule the session itself is read by: a
member's own, and every one for an admin of the org. In a held org, where
self-serve signups land beside the platform's staff, a session is its
person's alone.

parameters.name: id

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
After pages forward through the session's events starting strictly after

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit bounds how many events recentEvents carries (1..1000; default 50 on a
tail read, or 200 when paging forward with after).

patch.summary: Updates a session's surface-owned truth: its status, its title, the run-target it is dispatched to, and the product it built plus whether that build's story is public.
patch.description:
Updates a session's surface-owned truth: its status, its title,
the run-target it is dispatched to, and the product it built plus whether that

post.summary: Answers a question a session's run asked its person — a coding run's harness, or a turn of the app's conversation asking whether a coding run may start — from the page the session is read on.
post.description:
Answers a question a session's run asked its person — a coding
run's harness, or a turn of the app's conversation asking whether a coding run
may start — from the page the session is read on. The run waiting on it goes on
with the answer. Only the person the question is for may answer, once: a

parameters.name: id

post.description:
Sets, raises, or removes a session's cap.

  - a replacement must be strictly greater than what the session has consumed
  - removal is one-way: a session whose cap was removed cannot take one again,
    and a session created without one cannot be given one
  - raising or removing the cap resumes work that paused at it

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session, from the path.

get.summary: Returns the steering commands (pause/resume/stop/message) recorded against the caller's own session that are newer than the cursor, oldest first, with the cursor to poll from next.
get.description:
Returns the steering commands (pause/resume/stop/message)
recorded against the caller's own session that are newer than the cursor,
oldest first, with the cursor to poll from next. It is how a locally started
`hanzo code` session — which is not task-backed, so nothing forwards its
commands to an execution engine — consumes what the dashboard posted. Read-only
and bounded at 200 per poll, so a steady poll is cheap and an applied command is
never redelivered.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session whose commands are being drained, from the path.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
After is the last seq this poller applied; only commands newer than it come
back. Absent or negative reads as 0, which drains from the beginning.

get.summary: Reads a session's log in order, a page at a time: everything after the seq a reader last saw, so a poll resumes exactly where it stopped.
get.description:
Reads a session's log in order, a page at a time: everything after the seq a
reader last saw, so a poll resumes exactly where it stopped. It is how to see
what a run did and why it ended — each model turn, tool call, status and log
line, as the run wrote them. A run whose process went away is ended first,
with its reason as the last event.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to read, from the path.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
After is the seq of the last event already read; the page starts after it.
Absent or zero starts at the first event.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the page. Absent, zero or over 1000 reads as 200.

post.summary: Records one turn of a session's transcript and answers 201 with it.
post.description:
Records one turn of a session's transcript and answers 201 with it.

A `progress` turn additionally MOVES THE SESSION'S PROGRESS, marked as the run's
own word rather than an estimate, and pushes the updated session onto the live
stream — so a board's bar follows the run without polling and without a second
write path. See progress.go.

THE TURN IS SCANNED BEFORE IT IS STORED. The same engine the code-security
surface runs reads the payload at this boundary, and a credential in it refuses
the append with 422 rather than redacting it — a redacted transcript is one
that still had the secret in it once, and this way the author learns which
value to rotate. The refusal carries every finding: the rule, the severity, the
line, a MASKED preview and the fingerprint. The secret is never in the answer.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to append to, from the path.

post.summary: Sends a steering message to a running session — the endpoint a human or another agent interrupts through.
post.description:
Sends a steering message to a running session — the endpoint a
human or another agent interrupts through. It requires a `message` or a
`payload`; the other three commands do not.

A chat turn's run READS it: the message is handed to the model as the person's
next words at its next step, and a message that arrives while the model is
writing its answer gets a step of its own before the answer stands. A turn that
has already answered takes no more and answers 409 — what is said after an
answer is a new turn.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to steer, from the path.

post.summary: Asks a running session to pause.
post.description:
Asks a running session to pause. Recorded durably, and forwarded
to the durable-execution engine when the session is task-backed.

A chat turn's run is paused where it runs: it stops, the session stays live as
`paused`, and its sandbox is PARKED — the pod stops and every file stays, with
nothing billed for compute — until a resume picks it up.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to steer, from the path.

get.summary: Returns how far along one run is: the share of its goal that is done, whether it is running, blocked or finished, and a line saying what it is doing right now.
get.description:
Returns how far along one run is: the share of its goal that
is done, whether it is running, blocked or finished, and a line saying what it
is doing right now.

It is a MODEL ESTIMATE read off the run's own transcript, not a measurement —
`estimated` says so on every answer, and a run whose progress cannot be told
reports phase "unknown" with no percentage rather than a zero it does not
mean. A session that has already finished answers from its own status instead,
and is marked not estimated.

The list and detail reads carry the same value; this address is the one that
WAITS. Where the stored estimate has gone stale it is remade before answering,
so a human deciding whether to step into a run gets a current reading rather
than the last poll's — which costs one small completion, charged to the same
wallet the session already names, at most once every thirty seconds per run.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to act on, from the path.

post.summary: Asks a paused session to continue, on the same terms as a pause.
post.description:
Asks a paused session to continue, on the same terms as a pause.

A chat turn that was paused or STOPPED runs again: the same session, in the same
sandbox with every file it had written, told `message` next ("Continue where you
left off." when there is none). Only the person whose turn it was may resume
it, since the agent runs as them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to steer, from the path.

post.summary: Ends a running session.
post.description:
Ends a running session. `message` is recorded as the cancellation
reason, which is what a later reader of the transcript sees.

STOPPING IS NOT DELETING: the session, its transcript and anything it produced
stay readable. A session that has already finished is 409 rather than a second
stop.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to steer, from the path.

get.summary: Returns the subagent-flow graph rooted at this session: the session, its children, their children, each node carrying its own event count.
get.description:
Returns the subagent-flow graph rooted at this session: the session,
its children, their children, each node carrying its own event count. One
indexed read pulls the whole flow (every node of a flow shares a root id), so
the shape is assembled in memory rather than by walking the store per node. It
holds the sessions the caller may see — a member's own, every one for an admin
of the org — and a session they may not see is absent with all beneath it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the session to act on, from the path.

get.summary: Returns every machine registered to the caller's org, newest first, each with its live session load.
get.description:
Returns every machine registered to the caller's org, newest
first, each with its live session load. In a held org, where self-serve
signups land beside the platform's staff, it is only the caller's own.

post.description:
Registers a machine as an agent target, or re-links one that is
already registered. Re-linking is idempotent and keyed on org+host+owner, so a
machine that reconnects refreshes its own row rather than piling up duplicates;
it answers 200, while a first registration answers 201.

delete.description:
Deregisters one machine. Only its owner, or an org admin, may
remove it; an unknown id, a cross-org id and a machine owned by someone else
all answer the same not-found, so a probe learns nothing about what exists.

get.description: Returns one registered machine, with its live session load.

parameters.name: id

Updates one machine in place. Every field is optional; a field the
request omits is left alone. A metrics patch IS a heartbeat — the server stamps
its own clock, so a client can neither forge nor backdate staleness.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to update, from the path.

post.summary: ClaimRoutedRun is the machine's long poll for work: it authenticates the daemon, stamps the liveness the dispatch gate reads (the poll IS the proof a runner is listening), and waits up to 25 seconds for the next run addressed to THIS machine.
post.description:
ClaimRoutedRun is the machine's long poll for work: it authenticates the
daemon, stamps the liveness the dispatch gate reads (the poll IS the proof a
runner is listening), and waits up to 25 seconds for the next run addressed to
THIS machine. It answers the run when one arrives and 204 with no body when the
window elapses, on which the daemon re-polls immediately.

TWO independent proofs are required and both fail closed to the same 403: the
caller must own this machine (or be an org admin) AND present its claim key in
X-Target-Key. A run offered to one machine is unreachable from another's claim.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to act on, from the path.

delete.summary: Ends a folder's grant on this machine.
delete.description:
Ends a folder's grant on this machine. Only the machine's owner
may revoke, from the machine or the web. The machine reads its folders on
every heartbeat and drops this one, and a queued run in it is refused when
the machine claims it. A folder with no active grant is 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the machine, from the path.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description:
Folder is an absolute path on the machine, as its own file system spells
it. It is kept lexically clean, and a path with a `..` segment or that is
not absolute is refused.

get.description:
Returns the folders of this machine the web may start runs in:
the picker's choices. Anyone who can see the machine may read them.

post.description:
Lets runs started from the web work in one folder of this
machine and every folder under it. Only the machine's owner may grant, from
the machine itself (the desktop or `hanzo link grant`); another member gets
403. Granting a folder already granted answers that grant with 200; a new one

parameters.name: id

post.description:
Mints (or rotates) the claim key a `hanzo code --serve`
daemon presents to claim work for this machine, and returns it ONCE: only its
SHA-256 hash is stored. Rotating supersedes any prior daemon, so only the
machine's owner — or an org admin — may call it; every other caller gets the
same not-found an unknown id gets, and learns nothing about what exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the target to act on, from the path.

post.summary: Completes a claimed run: it delivers the terminal result to the run's durable owner, which is what lets that workflow finish.
post.description:
Completes a claimed run: it delivers the terminal result to the
run's durable owner, which is what lets that workflow finish. Scoped to (org,
target, run) and claim-key authenticated, so a machine can only ever report a
run it legitimately holds. Idempotent — a report for an unknown or
already-finished run answers delivered:false rather than failing, because the
session's terminal state was already set by the machine's own stream.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the machine reporting, from the path.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: RunID is the routed run being completed, from the path.

post.summary: Says one thing in the app's conversation and starts the turn that answers it.
post.description:
Says one thing in the app's conversation and starts the turn that
answers it. It answers at once with the conversation and the turn's run; the
turn itself is read from the session (GET /v1/agent/sessions/{id}, and its
?root= stream): the person's words, what the agent is doing, the coding runs it
starts, a question it asks, and its answer.

With no `session` it starts a conversation. With one it continues that
conversation in the same session, under a new run, once its last turn has
answered: 409 while a turn is still answering — what is said then is that
turn's next input (POST /v1/agent/sessions/{id}/message). A conversation is its
person's alone: anyone else's answers as absent, and a SuperAdmin acting in an
org that is not their own holds none there (their sandbox and builds would be
paid by that org).

Nothing is leased to answer: a turn that only talks uses no sandbox. Code is
worked on by a coding run — `dev`, with its own tools — which leases the
conversation's sandbox on the first build; a later one works on the
conversation's repository and carries on its last run, in that run's sandbox
and on its branch.

example.input: make the landing page load faster

delete.description: Removes an agent and every run recorded against it. Answers 204.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
Ref is the agent's public id (the agent_… handle create and list return) or
its org-unique name, from the path. Either resolves the same agent.

get.summary: Returns one agent with its system prompt and the caller's own 20 most recent runs of it: a run's input and output are its person's.
get.description:
Returns one agent with its system prompt and the caller's own 20 most
recent runs of it: a run's input and output are its person's.
The ref is the agent's public id or its org-unique name — a created agent is
immediately gettable by whatever create handed back.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
Ref is the agent's public id (the agent_… handle create and list return) or
its org-unique name, from the path. Either resolves the same agent.

patch.description:
Changes an agent in place. Every field is optional; a field the
request omits keeps its stored value. The resulting mode+schedule are
re-validated together, so a partial update can never leave a long-running
agent without the cron the scheduler needs to fire it, and a transition INTO
long-running counts against the per-org cap on scheduled agents.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the agent to update — its public id or org-unique name, from the path.

post.summary: Run one of your org's agents and get the recorded run back.
post.description:
Composes the agent's stored instructions with the caller's `input`, executes one real chat completion through the same in-process AI client the rest of the console uses, and answers with the run that was recorded: its id, status, model, output, duration and error. Every run this returns reflects an execution that actually happened — a model failure is recorded and reported, never hidden and never fabricated. A transient upstream failure (429, 5xx, empty choices) is retried up to three times with jittered backoff, and a configured failover model is tried before the run is called an error.

`ref` is the agent's public `agent_…` id or its org-unique name; either resolves the same agent, and it must belong to the caller's org, so an agent in another tenant is a 404 exactly like one that does not exist. A validated principal is required and the check is made twice on purpose: this route MOVES MONEY, so the debit's principal requirement is asserted where the money moves rather than inherited from the tenant lookup.

The org's balance is authorized BEFORE any inference, so an unfunded tenant gets 402 and no free compute, and a billing plane that cannot answer gets 503 rather than a free run. The flat per-run fee is an operator knob; setting it to zero makes runs free and removes the balance gate with them. Only a SUCCESSFUL run is billed, attributed to the model actually used — a failover run bills the model it fell over to, not the one it started on. A deployment with no inference wired answers 503 before any of this.

THE RULE A READER GETS WRONG: a failed run is a 502 whose body is the RUN, not an error envelope. The execution happened, the run was persisted to this agent's history, and its `error` field is the product — so a client that treats every non-2xx as an opaque failure throws away the only account of what went wrong. Each run also opens a root session in the live session registry, best-effort: a bookkeeping failure there never fails the run, because the run and its billing already happened.

get.summary: Returns the caller's own runs of one agent, newest first — each run's input, its output or its error, and how long it took.
get.description:
Returns the caller's own runs of one agent, newest first — each
run's input, its output or its error, and how long it took. A run is the
person's who asked for it, so another member's runs are not listed, nor an
org admin's view of them; a run no person asked for (a schedule) is listed to a
SuperAdmin alone. Every row is a run that actually happened.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the agent's public id or its org-unique name, from the path.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps how many runs come back, newest first. Absent, zero or out of
range (1..200) reads as 50.

get.summary: Answers what one of your org's agents has spent, in integer micro-USD.
get.description:
Answers what one of your org's agents has spent, in integer micro-USD.

It answers the agent's budget — `cap_micro_usd` per `period`,
`max_task_micro_usd` per run — with what the current period has consumed,
what remains, and `by_component`: the spend attributed to `model` (every
completion the agent bought), `computer` (the runtime it was resident for)
and `tool`. A component with no spend is absent, not zero. Every amount is an
integer number of micro-USD (1,000,000 = $1); 11902000 is $11.902. Pass
`by=component` to ask for the breakdown by name — it is the one grouping, and
the default.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Ref is the agent's public id or its org-unique name.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: By groups the answer: "component" is the only grouping today.
