openQuestions.description: OpenQuestions are the unresolved questions surfaced for domain review or follow-up.

question.description: Question is the nonconfidential research question assigned to the venture lead.

rerunsPerformed.description: RerunsPerformed is how many failed specialist tasks were re-executed on the latest rerun.

skippedCompleted.description: SkippedCompleted is how many already-completed specialist tasks were preserved without re-running on the latest rerun.

status.description: Status is the brief's lifecycle state: completed or partial_failure.

synthesis.description: Synthesis is the lead agent's integrated synthesis once all specialist child tasks succeed.

tasks.description: Tasks are the durable specialist child tasks belonging to this brief.

title.description: Title is the short headline of the research brief.

totalMicroUsd.description: TotalMicroUSD is the total spend across all specialist tasks and the lead synthesis in integer micro-USD.

unsupportedClaims.description: UnsupportedClaims are the claims flagged as lacking primary empirical support.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when the brief was last updated, as Unix seconds.

venture.description: Venture is the venture slug this research brief belongs to.

agentId.description: AgentID is the specialist agent's stable handle (`agent_...`).

agentName.description: AgentName is the specialist agent's name in the organization.

attempts.description: Attempts counts how many times this specialist task has been executed.

briefId.description: BriefID is the parent research brief identifier (`brief_...`).

citations.description: Citations are the source references extracted from the specialist's output.

error.description: Error records the failure reason when status is "error".

function.description: Function is the studio function the specialist represents.

id.description: ID is the stable task identifier (`task_...`).

lineage.description: Lineage is the specialist's ancestor agent IDs, nearest first.

microUsd.description: MicroUSD is the cumulative spend of this child task in integer micro-USD.

output.description: Output is the attributable text produced by the specialist when status is "done".

parentId.description: ParentID is the manager agent ID in the specialist's lineage.

prompt.description: Prompt is the specialist-scoped sub-brief dispatched to this agent.

runId.description: RunID is the recorded agent_runs row ID for the latest execution attempt.

status.description: Status is the durable task state: pending, done, or error.

unsupportedClaims.description: UnsupportedClaims are the claims the specialist flagged as lacking primary evidence.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when the child task was last updated, as Unix seconds.

ok.description: OK means the operation was accepted; it does not imply that an associated coding run has finished.

queued.description:
Queued says the instruction was kept and the run has not taken it yet: it is in the
run's inbox, and is delivered when the run's owner reads it. Absent, the run has it.

artifacts.description: Artifacts are the run's artifacts, stored files first. Never null.

saved.description:
Saved is when the artifacts were saved, RFC 3339 in UTC; empty while the run
has saved none.

binary.description: Binary marks content that is not text; it comes back base64.

content.description: Content is the file's bytes, empty when Truncated.

encoding.description: Encoding is how Content is carried: "utf8" verbatim, or "base64".

path.description: Path is the file's repo-relative path.

size.description: Size is the file's byte length in the repository, whatever was returned below.

truncated.description: Truncated marks a file past the 1 MiB view cap. No content is sent.

base.description:
Base is the branch the run started from: the one it was given, or the
repository's default.

commits.description: Commits are the commits on head that base does not have, newest first.

files.description:
Files is the net change head makes against its merge base with base, one
entry per file.

head.description: Head is the run's own branch. Empty for a plan or a setup, which write none.

moreCommits.description:
MoreCommits says the branch carries more commits than the newest 250 that
Commits lists.

moreFiles.description:
MoreFiles says the change is larger than one read answers — past 8 MiB of
diff or 3000 files — so Files lists the files before that, and the last of
them is marked truncated with the counts of the part read.

pull.description:
Pull is the run's pull request, or null while it has none. The forge's own
is read whole; one proposed somewhere else — a repository the forge only
mirrors from GitHub — is the address and number the run recorded, with its
state, title and reviews empty.

repo.description: Repo is the run's repository on the forge, owner/name.

steers.description:
Steers are the instructions said to the run while no pod held it, oldest
first, each queued until the run took it and delivered after. An instruction
that reached a run directly is not here: its answer was the delivery.

author.description:
Author is the commit author's name as git recorded it; a run's own commits
are authored by its harness.

date.description: Date is the author date, RFC 3339 in UTC.

message.description: Message is the commit's subject — its first line only.

sha.description: SHA is the full commit hash.

name.description: Name is the entry's own name, no directory part.

path.description: Path is the entry's full repo-relative path.

size.description: Size is a file's byte length; 0 for a directory.

type.description: Type is "tree" for a directory and "blob" for anything else a reader opens.

requestId.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this request the same request: the time is added
once, and the retry answers what the first answered. The Idempotency-Key
header is the same value, and wins when both are sent. Optional.

seconds.description:
Seconds is how much to add to the time the run is held to. It is added to
what the run has left, up to the longest a run may be given, so asking for
more than that is answered with what the run got.

session.description: Session is the run's handle, from the path.

seconds.description: Seconds is how long the run has left.

until.description: Until is when the run is ended for time now, as an RFC 3339 time.

additions.description:
Additions counts the lines the change adds, over the whole file whether or
not all of its patch is carried.

deletions.description: Deletions counts the lines the change removes, the same way.

from.description: From is where a renamed file was. Omitted for every other status.

patch.description:
Patch is the file's unified-diff hunks, from its first "@@". Empty for a
binary file and for a rename that moved no line.

path.description: Path is where the file is on the branch — for a deleted file, where it was.

status.description: Status is added, modified, deleted or renamed.

truncated.description:
Truncated marks a patch cut short: at 64 KiB for one file, or past 1 MiB of
patch across the change, when later files carry none. The counts are whole.

requestId.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this merge the same merge, answered as the first
was. The Idempotency-Key header is the same value, and wins when both are sent.
Optional.

session.description: Session is the run's handle, from the path.

base.description: Base is the branch it was merged into.

number.description: Number is the pull request's number in its repository.

url.description: URL is where it is read.

mergeable.description:
Mergeable is the forge's verdict that the base takes the branch without
conflict.

moreReviews.description: MoreReviews says it has more reviews than the first 50 that Reviews lists.

number.description: Number is the pull request's number in its repository.

reviews.description: Reviews are its reviews, oldest first: the first 50.

state.description: State is open, closed or merged.

url.description: URL is where a person reads and merges it.

assignees.description:
Assignees are the GitHub logins it is assigned to. GitHub repositories only;
a forge repository ignores them.

base.description: Base is the branch to propose into. Empty is the branch the run started from.

body.description:
Body is its description. Empty says who it is for, the task, the branch and
the run it came from.

draft.description: Draft opens it as a draft, which a reviewer cannot merge until it is ready.

requestId.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this request the same request, answered as the
first was. The Idempotency-Key header is the same value, and wins when both
are sent. Optional.

reviewers.description:
Reviewers are the GitHub logins asked to review it. GitHub repositories
only; a forge repository ignores them.

session.description: Session is the run's handle, from the path.

title.description: Title is the pull request's title. Empty takes one from the run's task.

base.description: Base is the branch it proposes into.

number.description: Number is the pull request's number in its repository.

url.description: URL is where it is read.

warning.description:
Warning says what was asked and not done: the pull request is open, but an
assignee or reviewer GitHub refused (not a collaborator, say) was not added.

at.description:
At is when it was submitted, RFC 3339 in UTC; empty for one that has not
been.

author.description: Author is the reviewer's forge login.

body.description:
Body is what the reviewer wrote; empty for a bare verdict. At most 16 KiB
of it, and 256 KiB across the reviews listed.

state.description:
State is the verdict: approved, request_changes, comment, pending or
request_review.

truncated.description:
Truncated marks a Body cut at either bound — or left empty past the second,
where the review keeps its author, verdict and time.

after.description:
After names a previous run's session, and starts this one from where that
one stopped instead of from the repository's default. It is how a follow-up
instruction — "now add tests for it" — builds on work already done rather
than beginning again on a fresh clone: the follow-up resumes the earlier
run's sandbox and works in its tree, files, installs and all, while that
sandbox is kept; one reaped by then is cloned again from the earlier branch.

The follow-up writes the SAME branch the earlier run did, on top of its
commits, so one piece of work is one branch and one pull request however
many instructions it takes. It pushes without force, so it only ever adds to
that branch. When the earlier run was on another repository, or kept its work
local, there is no branch to carry on and the follow-up writes a new one.
Branch names the branch instead.

A caller who already knows the branch may pass Base directly. Base wins if
both are given.

agentRef.description:
AgentRef names a configured agent to run as, which is how an org pins a
harness, a model and a prompt to a name. Empty runs the default agent.

assignees.description:
Assignees are the GitHub logins the pull request Pull asks for is assigned
to. GitHub repositories only; a forge repository ignores them.

base.description:
Base is the branch to start from. Empty takes the repository's default. The
run never writes here — it writes the agent branch it answers with.

branch.description:
Branch names the branch the run writes, as `agent/<name>`: pass the name
alone, or with the prefix. Runs write only under `agent/`, never to Base or
to the default branch, so the name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.
Empty takes `agent/` and the first part of the run's session id, or the
earlier run's branch when After names one.

A branch that already exists on the repository is carried on, not replaced:
the run starts from it and adds commits, and its pull request is the one it
already has.

conversation.description:
Conversation is the Dev conversation this run is part of (POST
/v1/agent/turns): one of the caller's own. The run is held in its tree, so it
is read, steered and written as the conversation is — by its person alone.
The app writes it; a run that carries on one in a conversation (After) is in
that conversation without naming it. Empty is a run of its own.

desktop.description:
Desktop asks for a run with a SCREEN — an image carrying an X server — for a
task that has to drive a browser or another windowed program. False, the
default, is a headless checkout, which is what writing code needs.

developerInstructions.description:
DeveloperInstructions is the explicit alias for Instructions passed to the
coding harness as developer_instructions; optional.

dir.description:
Dir is the folder on that machine the run works in: an absolute path inside
one of the folders the machine's owner has let the web use (the target's
`folders`). A folder outside every grant is refused 403
`folder_not_granted`, and the machine checks the real path again before it
runs. It needs TargetID and is a run on no repository: a run works in a
repository or in a folder of the machine, not both. Empty is the machine's
own choice.

draft.description: Draft opens the pull request Pull asks for as a draft.

effort.description:
Effort is how hard that model reasons: low, medium or high. Empty takes the
model's own default. Taken by the dev and codex harnesses, like Model.

issue.description:
Issue is the issue this run resolves: its number on Repo (`464` or `#464`),
or `owner/name#464` for an issue in another repository. Its pull request
says `Closes <issue>`, so merging the work closes the issue. Empty, or 0, is
a run no issue asked for.

mode.description:
Mode is what the run may do to the repository: `build` edits, commits and
pushes its branch; `plan` reads the repository and answers with a plan,
writing nothing — its sandbox is handed a credential that can only read and
no push step runs, and the plan arrives as the run's final status. `setup`
is a plan put to one question: its agent explores the checkout, installs and
checks what it finds, and ends with the codebase's environment, which is kept
as the proposal at /v1/environment/{repo} until someone saves it. Empty is
`build`. A plan or a setup runs in our sandbox only: a claimed machine clones
and pushes with its own credential, so one routed to a machine is refused.

model.description:
Model is the model the run's agent thinks with, by the id GET /v1/models
lists. Empty takes the platform's coding model. The dev and codex harnesses
take it; the others do not think with a model we name, so naming one for
them is refused.

project.description:
Project scopes the run to one board's work when the org keeps more than one.
Empty is the org's default.

prompt.description:
Prompt is the task, in the words you would use with a colleague who has the
checkout open. It is the whole instruction: there is no second field for
context, and a prompt that names files and the outcome it wants gets a run
that does not have to guess either.

pull.description:
Pull is whether the run opens a pull request for what it pushed. Unset, it
pushes the branch and opens none: a pull request is the step after the work,
taken when it is ready, and a run resumed with `after` adds to the same branch.
True opens one when the run changed something.

readOnly.description:
ReadOnly asks for a routed run whose harness may not write to the granted folder
or checkout, commit, push or open a pull request. It needs a targetId: our own
sandbox already hands plan runs a read-only credential, so use `mode: plan` for
those. A target whose machine does not advertise readOnlyRuns is refused with
422 read_only_unsupported before a session is opened. Absent is today's writable
run. This contains one harness run; it is NOT a promise about the machine itself.

reply.description:
Reply is WHERE THE RUN NARRATES ITSELF, when the surface that started it has
somewhere for it to talk. Empty means nobody is listening and the run simply
does not narrate — which is the app surface's case, because /v1/agent/coding
hands back a session id and the session stream is a better progress feed than
any message could be.

IT IS NOT A FIELD A MODEL FILLS IN. A run asked for in a conversation is
dispatched with the address that conversation is happening at, written over
whatever arrived here (apps/agents/replyto.go). A model naming a channel is
a model naming a channel it was not spoken to in, so the value it chose is
discarded rather than argued with — which is the same rule that left the org
and the subject off this type entirely.

repo.description:
Repo is what to work on: a repository's name, `owner/name` in the caller's
own org, or the site a repository serves (`hanzo.ai`), as the person said
it. The engine resolves it against the org's own repositories — a name that
matches none is refused with the nearest ones — and finds the clone URL and
the push credential from the org itself, so this says WHICH repository and
never how to reach it.

A repository on GitHub is named by GitHub's address, `github.com/owner/name`
— or `owner/name` when the owner is not the org's own — and runs there
directly: it is admitted when the caller's own connected GitHub may push to
it, or when the caller administers the org and the org's installation holds
it, and refused otherwise.

A repository the caller can read and not push to — a public repository, or
one their GitHub reads — is cloned read-only: the run works, commits in its
workspace, and pushes nothing; its change is kept as the run's artifacts.

Empty runs in an empty workspace: a fresh git repository in the sandbox,
with nothing cloned and nothing pushed.

requestId.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this request the same request: one run for this
caller whichever pod takes the retry and whatever restarts between, and the
retry answers what the first answered. The Idempotency-Key header is the same
value, and wins when both are sent. Optional.

reviewers.description:
Reviewers are the GitHub logins asked to review the pull request Pull asks
for. GitHub repositories only; a forge repository ignores them.

targetId.description:
TargetID routes the run to a registered machine the org has claimed instead
of to a sandbox in our cluster. Empty runs it here, which is the usual case.

task.description:
Task is Prompt under the name a caller asking for work tends to reach for.
The two are one field: Prompt wins when both are given.

timeoutSeconds.description:
TimeoutSeconds bounds the whole run. Unset takes the longest a run may take,
which is the longest a session may live (a day by default); a longer value
is that long. A run that hits the bound is stopped and reports what it had
done by then. A dev run's model credential is renewed for as long as it
lasts; a claude or codex run reads its credential once, so it ends a little
short of the four hours that credential is good for, saying so, with its
work kept on its branch.

tool.description:
Tool is which harness runs the prompt — dev | claude | codex | python |
node — and Desktop is whether the run needs a screen. Both are empty by
default, which is `dev` with no screen, and that default is what every
caller gets until it says otherwise.

They are two fields because they are two questions. The harness decides
what argv starts; the screen decides which image carries an X server. A
caller may want claude WITH a browser it can see, and a single enum would
have made that combination unsayable.

branch.description:
Branch is the ref the run will push its work to, and the ONLY ref it is
permitted to write. It exists before the work does, so it is safe to tell
somebody where to look while the run is still going.

carried.description:
Carried is how many of the instructions queued on the run `after` names went into
this run's task. Zero for a run that follows nothing, or one with nothing queued.

dropped.description:
Dropped is how many of them fit no task at all (more than the prompt limit) and were
set aside, not left queued.

left.description:
Left is how many of them did not fit this run's task and are still queued on the
run it follows.

note.description: Note says what became of the queue in words, when there was one.

pull.description: Pull is the CLI command or instruction to pull this run locally, e.g. `hanzo pull <sessionId>`.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository the run was admitted against, echoed back as the
engine resolved it.

routed.description:
Routed says the run went to one of the org's own registered machines rather
than to a sandbox in our cluster. False is the ordinary case.

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the run's handle: its durable record, and the root its live
progress streams under at /v1/agent/sessions/stream?root=<sessionId>. Every
later question about this run is asked with it.

targetId.description: TargetID names that machine when Routed is true, and is empty otherwise.

delivered.description: Delivered is when the run took it, empty while it is queued.

requestId.description: RequestID is the id the instruction was sent with, when it had one.

said.description: Said is when it was said, an RFC 3339 time in UTC.

state.description:
State is queued while the run has not taken the instruction, and delivered
once it has. An instruction queued for a run that ended stays queued: it was
never delivered, and a run started after it carries it. Dropped is one that fit
no task, which that start set aside.

entries.description: Entries are the directory's immediate children, directories first.

ref.description:
Ref is the branch this was read at: the run's own once the forge holds it,
its base until then.

cpuTemp.description: CPUTemp is the CPU package temperature in °C.

cpuUtil.description: CPUUtil is the busy fraction of all cores over the sample window, 0..1.

decode.description: Decode is generation throughput over the sample window, in tokens per second.

diskRead.description: DiskRead is the block-device read rate in bytes per second.

diskTotal.description: DiskTotal is the size of those filesystems, in bytes.

diskUsed.description: DiskUsed is the space used across local block filesystems, in bytes.

diskWrite.description: DiskWrite is the block-device write rate in bytes per second.

gpuMemTotal.description: GPUMemTotal is dedicated VRAM in bytes; absent when the GPU shares system memory (unified).

gpuMemUsed.description: GPUMemUsed is the memory held by GPU processes, in bytes.

gpuPower.description: GPUPower is the total GPU power draw in watts.

gpuPowerLimit.description: GPUPowerLimit is the total enforced GPU power limit in watts; absent when the driver reports none.

gpuTemp.description: GPUTemp is the hottest GPU's temperature in °C.

load1.description:
Load1 is the machine's own one-minute load average — a count of runnable and
uninterruptible tasks, NOT a percentage and NOT already divided by core
count, so it is read against Spec.CPUs: 8.0 is idle on 16 cores and swamped
on 4. Coerced finite and non-negative on write, so 0 means either genuinely
idle or nothing reported.

load15.description:
Load15 is the same figure over fifteen. The three together are what separate
a machine that is busy right now from one that has been busy all along —
which is the question a dispatcher is really asking.

load5.description: Load5 is the same figure averaged over five minutes.

model.description: Model is the model id(s) served on this machine, comma-separated, at most 128 bytes.

netRx.description: NetRx is the receive rate of physical interfaces in bytes per second.

netTx.description: NetTx is the transmit rate of physical interfaces in bytes per second.

prefill.description: Prefill is prompt (prefill) throughput over the sample window, in tokens per second.

running.description: Running is the number of requests being served now.

ttft.description: TTFT is the mean time to first token, in seconds, of requests that started in the window.

waiting.description: Waiting is the number of requests queued.

channel.description:
Channel is the conversation inside that workspace, and it is what decides whether
there is an address at all. Empty is the ordinary case: a caller of
/v1/agent/coding holds a session id and reads the stream instead.

provider.description:
Provider is the transport the conversation is on — slack, discord,
telegram, teams — and it is what decides who can carry the text at all. An
address without it names a channel in no particular workspace.

thread.description:
Thread narrows the address to one thread inside the channel — on Slack the
parent message's ts, the same value a reply carries as thread_ts. Empty
puts the text at the top level of the channel.

turn.description:
Turn is the turn that renders a run started here: the session whose one
message the run's progress and its outcome are shown in. A run with a Turn
posts nothing of its own — one question, one message. The dispatcher writes
it (apps/agents/replyto.go); a model never does.

user.description:
User is the platform's id for the person the conversation is with — whose
run it is. A run's buttons name them to anyone else who presses one; it is
never what decides who may (that is the chat identity).

estimatedMicroUsd.description: EstimatedMicroUSD is the estimated period cost for the proposed role in integer micro-USD.

examples.description: Examples lists concrete run IDs, unsupported claims, or reviewer corrections demonstrating the gap.

failureCount.description: FailureCount is how many repeated failures were observed in this area.

function.description: Function is the studio function where the coverage gap or failure occurred (e.g. "regulatory-clinical").

reportingLine.description: ReportingLine names the manager agent handle the proposed role will report to; defaults to "venture-lead".

reviewSeconds.description: ReviewSeconds is the human domain-review effort recorded on this gap in seconds.

roleName.description: RoleName is the suggested agent handle for the proposed specialist role; generated from Function and Topic when omitted.

title.description: Title is the human-readable title for the proposed role.

topic.description: Topic describes the missing expertise or recurring failure domain (e.g. "laboratory-lims-telemetry-integration").

agentId.description: AgentID is the created agent's handle (`agent_...`) once the proposal has been approved; empty when pending or rejected.

cap_micro_usd.description: CapMicroUSD is the period budget cap in integer micro-USD that will be set on the created agent.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the proposal was generated, as Unix seconds.

decidedAt.description: DecidedAt is when the proposal was approved or rejected, as Unix seconds.

decidedBy.description: DecidedBy records the subject who approved or rejected the proposal.

decisionReason.description: DecisionReason records the operator's note when approving or rejecting.

estimatedMicroUsd.description: EstimatedMicroUSD is the estimated monthly spend for this role in integer micro-USD.

examples.description: Examples are the concrete failed runs, unsupported claims, or review bottlenecks backing the proposal.

function.description: Function is the studio function this role candidate belongs to.

id.description: ID is the stable proposal identifier (`prop_...`).

instructions.description: Instructions is the system prompt that will govern the proposed role.

max_task_micro_usd.description: MaxTaskMicroUSD is the single-run budget ceiling in integer micro-USD that will be set on the created agent.

name.description: Name is the org-unique agent handle that will be created if the proposal is approved.

period.description: Period is the budget reset window: day, week, or month.

rationale.description: Rationale explains why the nightly review proposed this role candidate.

reportingLine.description: ReportingLine is the manager agent handle (`parent`) the proposed role reports to.

status.description: Status is the proposal's decision state: pending, approved, or rejected.

title.description: Title is the human-readable title of the proposed role.

tools.description: Tools are the MCP tool names the proposed role will be granted.

venture.description: Venture is the venture slug the role candidate is proposed for.

cap_micro_usd.description: CapMicroUSD is the period budget cap in integer micro-USD; defaults to the template's cap when omitted.

duties.description: Duties is the system prompt (instructions) governing the role's behavior and output.

expertise.description: Expertise is the catalog description explaining the role's domain expertise.

function.description: Function names the studio function ("lead" or one of the seven studio functions).

manager.description: Manager names the parent agent handle or id this role reports to in the org chart.

max_task_micro_usd.description: MaxTaskMicroUSD is the per-run budget ceiling in integer micro-USD; defaults to the template's ceiling when omitted.

model.description: Model optionally overrides the model this role runs on.

name.description: Name is the agent handle to create or update in the organization (e.g. "venture-lead" or "specialist-regulatory-clinical").

output.description: Output describes the required deliverable format for this role.

period.description: Period is the budget reset window (day, week, or month); defaults to "month".

schedule.description: Schedule is the 5-field cron expression when executionMode is "long-running".

sources.description: Sources lists the knowledge and evidence sources this role is permitted to query.

templateId.description: TemplateID optionally selects a shared RoleTemplate by id to inherit defaults from.

templateVersion.description: TemplateVersion records the explicit shared template version used for this role; defaults to StudioTemplateVersion.

tools.description: Tools lists the MCP tool names this role is allowed to call.

cap_micro_usd.description: CapMicroUSD is the default period budget cap in integer micro-USD.

expertise.description: Expertise is the one-line catalog description explaining when another agent or lead should delegate to this role.

function.description: Function is the studio function this role belongs to ("lead" or one of the seven studio functions).

id.description: ID is the stable template identifier (e.g. "venture-lead" or "specialist-regulatory-clinical").

instructions.description: Instructions is the system prompt governing how the role gathers evidence, cites sources, and flags unsupported claims.

manager.description: Manager is the default parent role handle this role reports to; empty for the venture lead.

max_task_micro_usd.description: MaxTaskMicroUSD is the default single-run ceiling in integer micro-USD.

output.description: Output specifies the structured deliverable format expected from this role.

period.description: Period is the budget reset window: day, week, or month.

sources.description: Sources lists the authorized evidence and knowledge sources for this role.

title.description: Title is the human-readable role title.

tools.description: Tools lists the MCP tool names this role is allowed to invoke.

version.description: Version is the explicit template revision string, preserved when a venture enrolls the role.

gpus.description:
GPUs is every accelerator the machine advertises, one entry each, capped at
32 on write. Empty means the probe found none — and that is the answer a
Need is checked against, so a machine with no entry here clears no
accelerator floor. The list is not vendor-filtered: what satisfies a job is
counts and VRAM, never a brand (see Need).

readOnlyRuns.description:
ReadOnlyRuns says this machine's harness can run one routed run against a
read-only workspace, without commit, push or PR, and refuses one it cannot
honour. Absent or false means unsupported: a read-only run is never sent here.
It is advertised by the harness itself, not inferred from os/arch/GPUs.

defaultOutput.description: DefaultOutput describes the required deliverable structure and citation standard.

defaultTools.description: DefaultTools lists the MCP tool names granted by default to specialists in this function.

duties.description: Duties states the core responsibilities and operating boundaries of the function.

expertise.description: Expertise summarizes the domain specialization covered by roles in this function.

id.description: ID is the stable slug identifying the studio function (e.g. "regulatory-clinical").

title.description: Title is the human-readable name of the studio function.

activity.description: Activity is the merged run/create/update events, newest first, capped at 50.

id.description:
ID identifies the event, and its shape says which kind it is: a run event
carries the run's own id, while an agent event is the agent id suffixed
":created" or ":updated". Unique within a feed, and not an address — there is
nothing to fetch it by.

message.description:
Message is the line to render, already bounded: "Invoked <model>" for a run
that worked, the run's own error truncated to 200 characters for one that did
not (or "Run failed" when it said nothing), and a fixed phrase for the two
agent events. Nothing here is invented — every event is a row that exists.

avatar.description:
Avatar is an image the agent is drawn as — a link to one, or the bytes
inline as a data URL, up to 96 KiB. Emoji is the one glyph a caller picked
when they had no image. At most one is ever set; neither means the agent is
drawn as its initial, the same way a person with no photo is. Both are
iam/pkg/schema's Mark, so a face means the same thing on an agent as it
does on a person or an org.
Avatar is the agent's picture: an image URL, or the image itself inline as a
data URL up to 96 KiB. Empty when the agent has no image.

avatar_licence.description:
AvatarLicence is the short name of the licence the avatar image is used
under ("Public domain", "CC0"). Present only with an avatar image.

avatar_source.description:
AvatarSource is the page the avatar image is described on, where its author
and licence can be read (a Wikimedia Commons file page, say). Present only
with an avatar image.

cap_micro_usd.description:
CapMicroUSD is the total this agent may spend within one Period, as an
integer number of micro-USD (1,000,000 = $1). It is required at creation: a
cap of zero would mean no limit and no per-agent spend record at all.

computeRef.description:
ComputeRef is the visor machine this bot is bound to, opaque here: this
package stores and echoes it, and the binding's lifecycle belongs elsewhere.
Empty means unbound, which is what every one-shot agent is.

consumed_micro_usd.description:
ConsumedMicroUSD is what has been spent in the current period, in micro-USD.
It is settled from what the gateway reported, not from the quote.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the agent was defined, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second.

description.description:
Description is the one line another agent reads when deciding whether to call
this one: the tool catalogue publishes it as the description of `agent_<name>`,
falling back to "agent <name>" when it is empty. It is not part of the prompt —
Instructions is — so writing the behaviour here reaches the caller and not the
model.

emoji.description:
Emoji is the single glyph a caller picked when they had no image. At most one
of avatar and emoji is ever set; neither means the agent is drawn as its
initial, the same way a person with no photo is.

executionMode.description:
ExecutionMode is one-shot or long-running, and it decides who may start this
agent. one-shot runs only when something POSTs to it; long-running is
additionally invoked by the scheduler on Schedule, once a minute against the
cron. An org's long-running agents are capped, so a switch INTO it can be
refused with 409.

groupId.description:
GroupID names the Bot Group ("grp_...") this bot belongs to when assigned to
a group; empty when unassigned.

id.description:
ID is the agent's stable handle, minted here as "agent_" + 32 hex characters
of crypto/rand. A caller cannot choose it, and it never changes — unlike Name,
which is the other way to address the same agent.

instructions.description:
Instructions is the agent's system prompt, verbatim, up to 32 KiB. It is the
one field the list read withholds, because it is the agent's whole behaviour
and a page of them would be a page of prompts.

isPrimary.description:
IsPrimary is true for the org's single Primary Bot (at most one per org,
default "hanzo") that directs subordinate bots and multi-layer Bot Groups.

layer.description:
Layer is the bot's tier in the coordination hierarchy: 0 for the Primary Bot,
1 for top-level group leads, and 2+ for nested worker and consensus bots.

lineage.description:
Lineage is every agent above this one, nearest first — the parent, its
parent, and so on to the agent a person defined. All of them are in this
org, so the principal this agent answers to is theirs.

max_task_micro_usd.description:
MaxTaskMicroUSD is the ceiling for a single run, in micro-USD. A session
cannot exceed it even when the period cap still has room, so one runaway
task cannot consume a month.

model.description:
Model is the Zen model this agent runs on, and it is always OUR name for it:
writes normalize through aimodel.ZenModel and the read normalizes again, so an
upstream family name never leaves here even from a row written before that
rule existed. A create that named none took the deployment's configured
default, so this is where a caller learns which model it actually got.

name.description:
Name is the agent's org-unique handle, matching
^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$. It addresses the agent everywhere ID does,
it is what a run row records, and it is the suffix of the `agent_<name>` tool
other agents call this one by. Set once at create; no update route moves it,
because moving it would orphan that history.

parent.description:
Parent is the agent that spawned this one; absent for an agent a person
defined.

period.description: Period is the window the cap resets on: day, week or month.

recentRuns.description:
RecentRuns is the agent's 20 most recent executions, newest first. It is a
window on the history, not the history: the count beside it is `runs`.

runs.description:
Runs is how many executions the org has recorded against this agent, counted
at read time. The list and update reads count the WHOLE history; the detail
read reports the size of the RecentRuns page it carries, which stops at 20 —
so a detail row saying 20 means "at least 20", not "exactly 20".

schedule.description:
Schedule is the 5-field cron the scheduler fires a long-running agent on,
evaluated once a minute. Required for long-running and DROPPED for one-shot —
a one-shot agent's schedule is not stored, so absence here is the mode's
answer rather than a value nobody set.

serviceAccountId.description:
ServiceAccountID is the IAM agent service account (<org>-<agent>) a scheduled
run is billed AS. It is what makes an autonomous run attributable to a
principal rather than only to the org; empty means the org itself wears the
spend.

status.description:
Status is the agent's readiness: "ready", or "retired" for a built-in whose
member has left Hanzo's team. A retired agent is left out of the list and
still answers a get by its handle. Server-set; no route accepts it.

tools.description:
Tools are the tool names this agent may call, and the list IS the authority:
an agent that declares none gets none. The single entry "*" means whatever the
fleet's MCP server serves at the moment of the run, resolved per run rather
than frozen here, which is how the default assistant reaches subsystems that
shipped after it was defined. Empty array, never null.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is the last time any field above was written, same format. It moves
on an update to the DEFINITION and never on a run, so a busy agent nobody has
edited keeps an old one.

agents.description: Agents is the org's agents, each carrying its recorded run count.

actor.description:
Actor is the "org/sub" identity the run was executed and billed AS. Empty
means there was no PERSON — a schedule or a service token — which is a
different fact from "we do not know", and the difference is what an audit
asks about.

agent.description:
What an operator needs to answer "what ran, for whom, and what did it do" —
and, through traceId, to leave this record for the waterfall of the very
same run rather than a search that hopefully lands near it.

Agent is on the row because the org-wide feed lists runs across agents, and
a run that cannot name its agent is an orphan in exactly the view built to
make sense of many of them. Every field but MicroUSD is omitempty: a run recorded
before these columns existed reports absence rather than a zero it never measured.

completionTokens.description:
CompletionTokens is the same measurement for what the model produced, on the
same final completion. It is a count of TOKENS, not of turns and not of money.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when the run finished, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second — the
duration above already says how long it had been going.

durationMs.description:
DurationMs is wall-clock milliseconds around the completion, including a
failover's retries. It is time SPENT, not time billed.

error.description:
Error is why an "ok"-less run failed, as the failing call reported it. Empty
on every successful run.

id.description:
ID is the run's handle, minted as "run_" + 32 hex characters. It is the key
the metering ledger records this run's per-round token spend under, so it is
how a bill and a run are joined.

input.description: Input is the text the run was given, verbatim.

micro_usd.description: MicroUSD is what the run spent, integer micro-USD: 0 for a run that cost nothing.

model.description:
Model is the model that actually SERVED this run, which is not always the one
the agent is defined on — a failover records what answered. Normalized to our
name on the way out; the stored row is left exactly as it happened, because a
run is a record and rewriting it would be worse than the name it carries.

output.description:
Output is what the model produced. Empty on an error run, and empty is also a
legitimate answer from a run that succeeded with nothing to say — Status is
what separates those.

promptTokens.description:
PromptTokens is what the gateway reported for the run's FINAL completion, and
only that one — a tool loop's earlier rounds are the metering ledger's account,
joined by this run's id. Reading it as the run's total spend undercounts a
loop.

status.description:
Status is the run's outcome, and there are exactly two: "ok" when the model
answered, "error" when it did not. It is written when the run ends, so no row
here is in flight.

toolCalls.description:
ToolCalls is how many tool dispatches the run made — a count of ACTIONS, which
is a different measurement from the token counts above and from the turns a
build reports. Zero is a run that answered straight from the model.

traceId.description:
TraceID is the trace this run IS, so the record and its spans are one thing to
move between: it opens the waterfall for THIS run rather than a search that
lands near it. Empty when the process had no tracer, never a fabricated id.
