chosen.description: Chosen says Text is one of the options the question offered.

id.description: ID is the session whose run asked, from the path.

question.description: Question is the question answered, as the session's `asked` status names it.

text.description: Text is the answer: a pressed option's label, or the person's own words.
Text is what it was answered with.

roles.description: Roles are the explicit role definitions to create or update in topological manager order.

seedDefaultSeven.description: SeedDefaultSeven, when true, seeds the default venture-lead and all seven studio function specialists before applying any custom roles in Roles.

templateVersion.description: TemplateVersion is the shared role template version to stamp on enrolled roles; defaults to StudioTemplateVersion.

venture.description: Venture is the venture slug this roster belongs to, used for attribution and metadata.

agents.description: Agents are the enrolled agent views in the organization after applying the roster.

created.description: Created is how many new agent roles were created by this call.

templateVersion.description: TemplateVersion is the shared template version applied.

updated.description: Updated is how many existing agent roles were updated idempotently in place without duplicating agents or budgets.

venture.description: Venture is the venture slug the roster was applied for.

model.description:
Model optionally sets the Zen model when creating the Primary Bot; defaults
to the deployment's chat model.

name.description:
Name optionally overrides the Primary Bot's handle when creating or promoting
one; defaults to "hanzo".

agent.description: Agent is the org's active Primary Bot (at Layer 0, isPrimary = true).

created.description:
Created is true when a new Primary Bot row was inserted by this call, and
false when an existing bot was returned or promoted.

briefs.description: Briefs are the organization's durable research briefs, newest first.

builds.description: Builds is every published build, most recently updated first.

agent.description: Agent is the label the surface that did the work calls itself by.

endedAt.description: EndedAt is when it finished, same format. Empty means it is still going.

org.description:
Org and Project are the build's public ADDRESS — the pair the full story is
read at, and the pair a visitor sees in the URL bar. Not a tenant key: this
index is anonymous and lists only what authors published.

project.description: Project is the product's slug, the second half of that address.

repo.description: Repo is the repository the work was done in, as the session reported it.

session.description:
Session is the agent session behind the build, and the value its commits name
in their `Hanzo-Session:` trailer.

startedAt.description: StartedAt is when the session opened, RFC 3339 in UTC.

status.description:
Status is the session's own: running, paused, done or error — so a card can
show a build still being written.

title.description:
Title is the human line for the card. Sent even when empty, like every field
here, because that is what this route has always sent.

turns.description:
Turns is HOW MANY turns the transcript holds — a COUNT, unlike the `turn` on
each turn of the full story, which is that turn's position. The full read
returns at most 1000 of them; this number is not capped.

actor.description:
Actor is who took the turn. A deploy turn's actor is the literal "deploy",
because nobody took it.

at.description: At is when the turn was recorded, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second.

body.description:
Body is the readable text of the turn, taken from the stored event's `text`.
Empty when the event carried a payload of some other shape — this route reads
transcripts and does not invent prose for turns that are not one.

commit.description:
Commit is the full sha this turn produced, empty when the turn changed
nothing. It is ECHOED from the transcript, and the authority is the commit
itself: it carries the `Hanzo-Session:`/`Hanzo-Turn:` trailer, or a note under
refs/notes/hanzo-provenance saying the same, so the claim is checkable at
source with the command in `verify`.

kind.description:
Kind is what the turn was, from the log's closed six: message, tool-call,
spawn, log, status, control. A deploy arrives as a `status` turn.

subject.description:
Subject is that commit's subject line, from the same transcript, so a reader
sees what the commit says without fetching the repository.

turn.description:
Seq is this turn's POSITION in the session's log — monotonic from 1, per
session — and it is what a commit's `Hanzo-Turn:` trailer names. It is not a
count of anything: the count is `turns` on the summary beside it.

agent.description: Agent is the label the surface that did the work calls itself by.

endedAt.description:
EndedAt is when it finished, same format. Empty means it has not — the build
is still going.

model.description:
Model is the model that did the work, taken from the FIRST turn whose body
names one — a transcript states it, this route does not resolve it. Empty when
no turn said.

org.description:
Org is the org that published this build, echoed from the URL. It is part of
the build's public ADDRESS and not a tenant key — this route is anonymous, and
the only rows it can reach are ones an author explicitly published.

project.description: Project is the product's slug, the other half of that address.

repo.description: Repo is the repository the work was done in, as the session reported it.

session.description:
Session is the id of the agent session this story IS — the same value a
produced commit carries in its `Hanzo-Session:` trailer, which is what ties
the repository's history to this page.

startedAt.description: StartedAt is when the session opened, RFC 3339 in UTC.

status.description:
Status is the session's own: running, paused, done or error. A build can be
read while it is still being written, so this is not always terminal — and an
`error` build is still a readable story, not a missing page.

title.description:
Title is the human line the session was opened or renamed with. Empty when
nobody gave it one.

turns.description:
Turns is the whole transcript, oldest first, capped at 1000: a published build
is a story to read down, not an archive to page.

verify.description:
Verify is the exact command that re-derives every commit binding below
straight from git, so nothing here has to be taken on trust.

claimKey.description:
ClaimKey is the capability itself. It is returned ONCE and never again — only
its SHA-256 hash is stored — so a daemon that loses it mints a new one.

targetId.description: TargetID is the machine the key authenticates.

requestId.description:
RequestID makes a retry of this instruction the same instruction: said once to
the run, whichever pod takes the retry and whatever restarts between. The
Idempotency-Key header is the same value, and wins when both are sent.
Optional.

session.description: Session identifies the running or paused coding session from the path.

text.description: Text is the new instruction to carry into the running turn or follow-up run.

command.description:
Command is what was asked, from a closed four: pause, resume, stop, message.
It is an INTENT — the poller decides what to do about it, and the session's
status changes only when the poller reports back that it did.

message.description:
Message is the text that came with the command: what to say into the run for
`message`, and the cancellation reason for `stop`. Up to 16 KiB. Empty on a
bare pause or resume.

payload.description:
Payload is the structured half a caller sent instead of (or beside) Message,
embedded as JSON. Its shape is the caller's business; this surface carries it
through untouched.

seq.description:
Seq is this command's position in the session's log — the same monotonic
number every other turn is ordered by, so a command sits in the transcript
where it was issued. Send the highest one you applied back as `after` and it
is never redelivered.

commands.description: Commands is the session's control commands newer than the cursor, oldest first.

cursor.description:
Cursor is the seq to send as `after` on the next poll — the highest seq in
this page, or the cursor sent in when the page is empty.

id.description: ID is the session to steer, from the path.

message.description:
Message is free text for the running agent, up to 16 KiB, scanned for
credentials before it is stored like the payload. On a stop it is recorded
as the cancellation reason.

payload.description:
Payload is a structured argument for the command: any valid JSON up to
64 KiB, scanned for credentials before it is stored (a hit refuses the
command with 422 and the findings). A task-backed session receives it as
the forwarded signal's argument.

command.description: Command is the verb that was recorded: pause, resume, stop or message.

event.description:
Event is the durable control event the command became. The intent is
recorded whether or not it reached an engine, which is what makes a
stream-consuming surface able to act on it.

forwarded.description:
Forwarded is whether the command also reached the durable-execution engine.
FALSE IS NOT A FAILURE: a session with no workflow link, or a deployment
with no tasks backend, is record-only by design. A forward that was
attempted and failed is a 502, never a false here.

run.description:
Run is the run a resume started, under the same session. Empty for every
other command.

avatar.description:
Avatar and Emoji are how the agent APPEARS. An image wins when both are
given — it is the thing somebody made — and both empty leaves the agent
drawn as its initial. Validated by iam/pkg/schema, the same rule a person's
avatar passes, so the 96 KiB bound and the accepted URL forms are stated
once for every subject that has a face.

avatar_licence.description:
AvatarLicence is the licence's short name, one line of up to 128 characters
("Public domain"). Like avatar_source, it is not stored without an avatar.

avatar_source.description:
AvatarSource is the https page the avatar image is described on, up to 2048
characters. It belongs to the image: without an avatar it is not stored.

cap_micro_usd.description:
The budget, required. An agent is not creatable without one: a zero cap
would mean no limit and no record of its spend, which is what a budget
exists to remove. Integer micro-USD; the CLI converts dollars before sending.

computeRef.description:
ComputeRef optionally binds this bot to a visor machine. Opaque here, bounded
at 256 characters, and not resolved — this package stores the reference and
the binding's lifecycle belongs elsewhere.

description.description:
Description is the one line published as the description of the `agent_<name>`
tool, which is how another agent decides whether to call this one. Optional,
and worth writing for exactly that reason.

emoji.description:
Emoji is the single glyph shown when there is no image. An image WINS when
both are given — it is the thing somebody made — and both empty leaves the
agent drawn as its initial.

executionMode.description:
ExecutionMode is one-shot or long-running. Empty takes one-shot, which runs
only when something POSTs to it. long-running additionally requires Schedule,
and counts against a per-org cap that answers 409 when it is full.

groupId.description:
GroupID optionally assigns this bot to an existing Bot Group (by grp_... id
or group name) at creation time.

instructions.description:
Instructions is the system prompt, up to 32 KiB, stored verbatim. This is what
the model reads; Description is what other CALLERS read.

isPrimary.description:
IsPrimary promotes this newly created bot to the org's sole Primary Bot
(Layer 0), atomically clearing isPrimary on any previous Primary Bot in the
org.

layer.description:
Layer sets the bot's coordination tier (0 for Primary Bot, 1+ for subordinate
layers).

max_task_micro_usd.description:
MaxTaskMicroUSD is the ceiling for a single run, in micro-USD. A session
cannot exceed it even when the period cap still has room, so one runaway
task cannot consume a month.

model.description:
Model names the model to run on. Omit it to take the deployment's configured
default; name one and it is checked against the gateway's served catalogue
here, so a model this deployment cannot serve is refused now rather than at
the first run. Stored under our own name for it, whatever spelling arrives.

name.description:
Name is the agent's org-unique handle and the only required field. It must
match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, and a name already taken in this org
is a 409 rather than an overwrite. It is permanent: no update route moves it.

parent.description:
Parent is the agent spawning this one — its id or name, in the caller's
org. The new agent answers to the org its parent answers to, and a parent
outside the caller's org is not found: an agent is never spawned into a
principal its creator does not answer to. Omitted for an agent a person
defines. Set once; no update moves it.

period.description: Period is the window the cap resets on: day, week or month.

schedule.description:
Schedule is the 5-field cron a long-running agent fires on, parsed here so a
bad expression is a 400 and not an agent that silently never runs. Required
with long-running; DISCARDED for one-shot rather than stored unused.

serviceAccountId.description:
ServiceAccountID optionally names the IAM agent service account (<org>-<agent>)
a scheduled run should be billed AS, so an autonomous run is attributable to a
principal rather than only to the org. Same 256-character bound, also
unresolved here.

tools.description:
Tools are the tool names this agent may call. Omitted or empty grants NONE —
that default is the agent's authority and is not widened anywhere. The single
entry "*" means whatever the fleet's MCP server serves at the time of each run.

description.description: Description explains what work this group handles for parent coordinators.

layer.description:
Layer places the group in the coordination hierarchy (defaults to 1, or
parent.Layer + 1 when parentGroupId is set).

members.description: Members lists the org's bot names or ids to assign to this group.

name.description: Name is the group's org-unique handle matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$.

parentGroupId.description:
ParentGroupID optionally nests this group beneath an existing parent group
(by id or name).

policy.description:
Policy configures how the group coordinates (defaults to quasar aurora when
omitted).

decision.description: Decision is the operator's verdict: "approve" (creates the agent role once) or "reject" (records rejection without creating an agent).

id.description: ID is the proposal handle (`prop_...`) from the URL path.

reason.description: Reason is an optional operator note explaining the approval or rejection.

actor.description:
Actor is who produced the turn. Empty takes the validated caller, which is
what an agent writing its own transcript wants; naming one is for a surface
recording on somebody else's behalf.

id.description: ID is the session to append to, from the path.

kind.description:
Kind is what this turn IS: message, tool-call, spawn, log, status, control
or progress. Anything else is refused — the vocabulary is closed so a
reader can branch on it.

payload.description:
Payload is the turn's own body, any valid JSON up to 64 KiB. It is SCANNED
for credentials before it is stored, and a hit refuses the whole append with
422 and the findings — this plane never redacts a secret into a transcript
it then keeps.

Its SHAPE is the writer's business for every kind but one: a `progress`
turn is the run reporting on itself in a shape this surface publishes —
{"pct":0-100 (optional), "phase":"queued|running|blocked|done",
"activity":"≤120 chars"} — so a malformed one is refused with 400 instead
of being stored as prose nobody reads.

events.description: Events is the page, in seq order.

next.description:
Next is the seq to pass as after for the page beyond this one; absent when
this page reached the end of the log as it stands now.

actor.description:
Actor is who produced the turn. A write that names nobody takes the calling
principal, so this is rarely empty in practice.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when the turn was recorded, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second. Seconds
are coarse enough that two turns can share one, which is why Seq and not this
is the order.

id.description:
ID is the event's own handle, minted as "evt_" + 32 hex characters. It
identifies the turn; Seq is what ORDERS it.

kind.description:
Kind is what the turn IS, from a closed six: message (a model turn),
tool-call, spawn (a subagent started), log, status, control (a steering
command the running surface consumes). Anything else is refused at the write.

payload.description:
Payload is the turn's body, embedded as JSON rather than as a string —
whatever the writer sent, up to 64 KiB, checked for well-formedness and
scanned for credentials before it was stored. Its SHAPE is the writer's
business and varies by Kind; this surface does not interpret it, except
that every string in it is kept as plain text: terminal escape sequences
and control characters other than the line break and the tab are removed.

seq.description:
Seq is the turn's position in this session's log: monotonic from 1, assigned
by the store inside the insert, and unique PER SESSION rather than globally.
It is the cursor a reader resumes from after a reconnect — ask for everything
after your last-seen seq.

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the session this turn belongs to. Carried on every event so a
stream frame stands alone — a subscriber watching a whole tree gets turns from
several sessions down one connection.

folder.description:
Folder is an absolute path on the machine, as its own file system spells
it. It is kept lexically clean, and a path with a `..` segment or that is
not absolute is refused.

id.description: ID is the machine, from the path.

folders.description:
Folders are the folders the web may start runs in on this machine, oldest
grant first.

folder.description: Folder is the folder that may no longer be used.

revoked.description: Revoked is true when an active grant was ended.

folder.description: Folder is the granted path. A run may work in it or in any folder under it.

grantedAt.description: GrantedAt is when, RFC 3339 in UTC.

grantedBy.description: GrantedBy is the machine's owner, who granted it.

groups.description: Groups is the org's Bot Groups ordered by layer ascending, then name.

alpha.description:
Alpha is the supermajority quorum fraction in (0, 1] required for a round to
lock on a candidate proposal (defaults to 0.67, i.e. 2/3, for quasar).

beta.description:
Beta is the number of consecutive quorum rounds required to finalize a Lux
Quasar certificate (defaults to 2).

confidenceFloor.description:
ConfidenceFloor is the minimum self-reported confidence in [0, 1] required by
the kai policy before accepting a consensus answer without escalation.

customRule.description:
CustomRule holds the natural-language adjudication rubric applied when kind
is custom.

escalateToPrimary.description:
EscalateToPrimary forwards deadlocked or low-confidence ballots to the org's
Primary Bot ("hanzo") for tie-breaking finality.

kind.description:
Kind selects the coordination mechanism: leader, quasar, majority, weighted,
unanimous, kai, or custom.

leader.description:
Leader names the bot that decomposes tasks and synthesizes member outputs
when kind is leader (or adjudicates when kind is custom).

maxBudgetMicroUSD.description:
MaxBudgetMicroUSD caps the combined spend of a single group run in integer
micro-USD when positive.

quasarProfile.description:
QuasarProfile selects a Lux Quasar preset (polaris, aurora, or pulsar) when
kind is quasar. Explicit sampleK, alpha, and beta values override the preset.

sampleK.description:
SampleK caps how many group members are sampled per consensus round (for
example 3 for polaris, 5 for aurora, 7 for pulsar). Zero samples all members.

weights.description:
Weights optionally overrides per-member voting weights for weighted and
quasar policies; unlisted members default to weight 1.0.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the group was created, RFC 3339 UTC.

description.description:
Description summarizes what the group owns so Primary Bot "hanzo" and parent
layers know when to delegate to it.

id.description: ID is the group's stable server-minted handle ("grp_" + hex).

layer.description:
Layer is the hierarchy tier (1 = direct report to Primary Bot "hanzo", 2+ =
nested sub-groups and specialist pools).

members.description: Members lists the bot names belonging to this group in deterministic order.

name.description:
Name is the group's org-unique handle, addressable as group_<name> in tools
and transport routing.

parentGroupId.description:
ParentGroupID names the parent Bot Group ("grp_...") when this group sits at
Layer 2 or deeper; empty means it reports directly to Primary Bot "hanzo".

policy.description:
Policy defines the leader, Lux Quasar, or voting consensus rules for this
group.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when the group definition was last updated, RFC 3339 UTC.

agent.description: Agent is the member bot's org-unique name.

choice.description:
Choice is the zero-based candidate index this member attested to in the final
ballot round.

confidence.description: Confidence is the member's self-reported certainty in [0, 1].

model.description: Model is the Zen model that served this member's turn.

proposal.description: Proposal is the candidate answer produced by this member bot.

runId.description: RunID is the recorded run_... handle of this member's execution.

status.description: Status is "ok" when the member answered or "error" when its turn failed.

weight.description: Weight is the effective voting weight applied to this member's ballot.

agent.description: Agent is the member bot's org-unique name or public agent_... id.

weight.description:
Weight is the non-negative voting multiplier assigned to this member (1.0 is
standard parity).

actor.description:
Actor is who produced the turn, defaulted to the calling principal when the
writer named nobody.

at.description: At is when the turn was recorded, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second.

kind.description:
Kind is what the turn was, from the log's closed six: message, tool-call,
spawn, log, status, control.

preview.description:
Preview is the first 240 bytes of the event's payload, cut without regard for
the JSON inside it — it is a string to SHOW, never a value to parse. Read the
detail or the stream for the whole payload.

seq.description:
Seq is that event's position in the session's log — monotonic from 1, per
session. A reader holding it can ask the detail or stream reads for
everything after it, so this doubles as the list's resume cursor.

resource.description:
Resource is the Resource Usage panel's rollup, and every field of it is
currently null — see resourceUsage. It is present rather than omitted so a
panel renders "—" instead of guessing.

cwd.description:
Cwd is where the session is working NOW.

It was write-once — captured at register and never again — which is right
for a run that starts in a directory and stays there, and wrong for a linked
shell, which is a place a person moves around in. The console showed the
directory `hanzo link` happened to be run from and kept showing it after the
shell had walked away, so the field answered "which work is this" with an
answer that was true once. A pointer, so an unchanged path is an omitted
field rather than a repeated write.

error.description:
Error is why the session ended in error: the exit status or refusal and the
last lines the process wrote. Kept only on a session in error.

id.description: ID is the session to update, from the path.

project.description:
Project tags the product this session built; Published is the author's
decision to let anyone read the story (provenance.go). Both are pointers so
"absent" and "cleared" are different requests.

published.description:
Published opens the session's story to the public build route; false withdraws
it, and withdrawing is always allowed. PUBLISHING is refused unless the
session names a Project — the one set in this same request, or the one already
stored — because that route is keyed on (org, project). It widens READ access
to what is already there and grants nothing else.

status.description:
Status moves the session to running, paused, done or error. A session that has
already finished refuses any change with 409 — done and error are monotonic —
and moving INTO one stamps the end time. This is the surface REPORTING what
happened; a control command never writes it.

target.description: Target re-dispatches a session to a run-target (the #48 association). "" detaches.

terminal.description:
Terminal publishes (or, with "", withdraws) the URL this session's live
terminal can be watched at. A pointer so "absent" and "withdrawn" are
different requests: a session that stops sharing must be able to say so.

title.description:
Title rewrites the human line, up to 512 characters — usually because the work
turned out to be something other than what it was opened as.

capacity.description: Capacity rewrites the human summary, up to 256 characters. "" clears it.

host.description:
Host re-points the hostname sessions are matched by. Moving it moves the load:
the session counts follow the new name from the next read.

id.description: ID is the target to update, from the path.

kind.description: Kind re-files it under laptop | cloud | gpu | cluster | machine.

label.description:
Label renames the machine, up to 128 characters. Empty STRING is refused — a
target with no name is a row nobody can pick out of a fleet.

metrics.description:
Metrics replaces the live sample, and sending one IS A HEARTBEAT: the server
stamps the time and appends the point to the fleet series. Sending an all-zero
sample CLEARS the heartbeat — the machine goes back to having no liveness fact
at all, and its stored status is taken at face value again.

spec.description:
Spec replaces the static capability whole, sanitized and clamped the same way
a register's is.

status.description:
Status sets operator INTENT: online | offline | draining. Draining is how a
machine is taken out of dispatch without ending what is already on it. What
comes back may still read offline, because the heartbeat outranks the intent.

proposals.description: Proposals are the matching role candidate proposals, newest first.

alpha.description: Alpha is the quorum threshold fraction required per round.

beta.description: Beta is the number of consecutive quorum rounds required for finality.

checkpointDigest.description:
CheckpointDigest is the 48-byte hex SHA3-384 cSHAKE256 commitment under
domain LUX-QUASAR-CHECKPOINT-V1 binding the threshold digest to the winning
output.

escalated.description:
Escalated is true when Primary Bot "hanzo" broke a tie after unfinalized
rounds.

finalized.description:
Finalized is true when the winning proposal held >= alpha support for beta
consecutive rounds.

profile.description: Profile names the active Lux Quasar profile (polaris, aurora, or pulsar).

rounds.description: Rounds is the total number of ballot rounds executed.

sampleK.description: SampleK is the validator sample size used per round.

support.description:
Support is the winning proposal's weighted vote share in [0, 1] on the final
round.

thresholdDigest.description:
ThresholdDigest is the 48-byte hex SHA3-384 cSHAKE256 commitment under domain
LUX-QUASAR-GROUPED-THRESHOLD-V1 over the round ballot tally.

account.description:
Account is which subscription or API account under that provider served the
run, up to 256 characters. It is what lets a revoke of that login stop exactly
the sessions it was paying for.

agent.description:
Agent is the label the surface opening this session calls itself by
("hanzo-dev"). REQUIRED, up to 128 characters, and free text — nothing
resolves it against a defined agent.

budget_micro_usd.description:
BudgetMicroUSD caps what this session may spend, integer micro-USD. Zero
means no cap; a cap can be raised or removed later, never added.

channel.description:
Channel is the collaborative channel this run was started in (HIP-0523), so a
space view can list the sessions of one channel. It is PROVENANCE and is set
only here: there is deliberately no way to move a session to another channel, so
it is absent from the patch input and from UpdateSession's SET list.

cwd.description:
Cwd is the directory the session starts in, up to 1024 characters. It can be
moved later, because a linked shell walks around.

host.description: Execution context — where this session runs (all optional).

parentSessionId.description:
ParentSessionID makes this a subagent of that session: it inherits the
parent's root, so one flow stays one tree. The parent must exist IN THE SAME
ORG — a foreign or unknown id is a 400, never a tree across tenants. Empty
opens a root session.

project.description:
The readable build (provenance.go): which product this session builds, and
whether its story may be read by the world.

provider.description: Account tag — the linked AI account this session ran under (login manager).

published.description:
Published opens this session's story to the public build route. It is refused
without a Project, because that route is keyed on (org, project) — a build
with no product is not a story anyone can open. False keeps it org-only.

repo.description:
Repo is the code being worked on, up to 512 characters. A label the surface
states; nothing resolves it against the forge.

status.description:
Status opens the session in one of running, paused, done or error. Empty means
running. A TERMINAL status here (done, error) records a session that has
already finished — its end time is stamped now — and nothing can move it
afterwards.

target.description:
Target names a run-target the org has registered. Unlike Host and Repo it IS
resolved: a target that does not exist in this org is a 400, so a session can
never claim to run on another tenant's machine. Empty names no machine.

taskRunId.description:
TaskRunID is that workflow's particular run, same bound. Recorded, not
resolved: this surface does not check the workflow exists.

taskWorkflowId.description:
TaskWorkflowID links this session to the hanzoai/tasks workflow that executes
it, up to 256 characters. Set it and control commands are forwarded to that
engine; leave it and the running surface polls for them instead.

terminal.description:
Terminal is the URL this session's live terminal is published at, so the
console can watch it. Optional — a session that publishes nothing is still
a session.

title.description:
Title is the human line a card shows, up to 512 characters. Optional, and
changeable later.

delivered.description:
Delivered is true when a waiting durable owner received this result. False
means there was none to deliver to — an unknown or already-finished run — which
is a clean no-op, not an error.

branch.description:
Branch, CommitSha and Diffstat describe what the run produced; Error is the
failure when OK is false. Each is clamped, never rejected.

changed.description:
Changed says whether the run produced any commit. It is INDEPENDENT of OK: a
run can succeed and change nothing (there was nothing to do), and a run can
fail after committing some of its work. Two questions, two booleans.

commitSha.description:
CommitSha is the tip the run pushed, clamped to 128 characters. Empty when it
pushed nothing, which is the same case Changed reports false for.

diffstat.description:
Diffstat is the run's own summary of what it changed, as text, clamped to
64 KiB. Free-form: it is shown, never parsed.

error.description:
Error is why the run failed, clamped to 64 KiB. It is CLAMPED rather than
refused — a truncated reason is worth more than a rejected report, because a
rejected report leaves the durable workflow waiting forever.

id.description: ID is the machine reporting, from the path.

ok.description: OK is whether the run succeeded; Changed whether it produced any commit.

runId.description: RunID is the routed run being completed, from the path.

costCents.description:
CostCents would be the window's spend in cents. Always null here — the money
a run costs is the metering ledger's, joined by the run id, and repeating it
from this side would be a second number that could disagree with the bill.

cpuVcpuHours.description:
CPUVcpuHours would be vCPU-hours over the window. Always null: this store
holds agent definitions and run I/O, and nothing here meters a CPU. Null is
the honest answer and 0 would be a claim.

memGbHours.description: MemGbHours would be gigabyte-hours of memory. Always null, same reason.

storageIoBytes.description:
StorageIoBytes would be bytes moved to and from storage. Always null, same
reason.

failureThreshold.description: FailureThreshold is the minimum number of failed runs on an agent or function that triggers a role proposal; defaults to 2.

observedGaps.description: ObservedGaps are explicit coverage gaps, unsupported-claim clusters, or review-effort spikes to evaluate alongside stored run history.

venture.description: Venture optionally scopes the nightly review to a specific venture slug.

created.description: Created is how many new role proposals were generated during this review pass.

proposals.description: Proposals are the active role candidate proposals resulting from the review.

functions.description: Functions are the seven canonical studio functions.

templates.description: Templates are the versioned role templates (lead plus the seven specialist functions).

version.description: Version is the current studio template catalog version string.

base.description:
Base is the branch to start FROM. Empty means the repository's default —
resolve it on the machine, since the machine is the one holding the clone.

branch.description:
Branch is the ref the run must push its work to, and the ONLY one it is
permitted to write: the forge's ref policy refuses anything else from this
run's credential. It is decided at dispatch and exists before the work does.

cloneUrl.description:
CloneURL is how to fetch the repository. It carries no credential: the
machine authenticates with the git identity it already holds, or with
DeployKey when the run has one.

deployKey.description:
DeployKey is the run's own key to its repository, when the repository is one
the machine cannot reach otherwise. It opens that one repository, is withdrawn
when the run ends, and is for the machine to use for the run and not keep.

dir.description:
Dir is the folder to work in, an absolute path inside one of the folders its
owner granted (the target's `folders`). The cloud checked the grant; the
machine checks the real path — symlinks and all — lies inside a folder it
still holds before it runs anything there. Empty is the machine's own choice.

effort.description:
Effort is how hard that model reasons: low, medium or high. Empty is the
model's own default.

instructions.description:
Instructions are the person's own instructions for their runs, as they set
them in their settings: the machine's harness reads them as its user's, the
way AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in its home is read. Empty when they set none.

knownHosts.description: KnownHosts is the forge's host key, to check the connection DeployKey opens.

model.description:
Model is the model the person asked the run's agent to think with, by the
id GET /v1/models lists. Empty is the machine's own default.

project.description:
Project is the product slug the run is filed under, so the machine can tag
what it produces. Empty when the dispatch named none.

prompt.description:
Prompt is the task, in full, as the person wrote it. There is no second field
for context.

readOnly.description:
ReadOnly tells the machine this run may not write to the granted folder or
checkout, commit, push or open a pull request: its answer is the run's terminal
status, reported with changed:false. The harness refuses the run if it cannot
honour it. This contains one run on the machine; it is not a security boundary
against the machine's owner. Not to be confused with DeployKey being read-only.

repo.description: Repo is the repository to work in and CloneURL is how to fetch it.

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the live session opened at dispatch; the machine streams its
turns into it.

timeoutSeconds.description: TimeoutSeconds bounds the run on the machine; 0 means the machine's own default.

input.description: Input is the task or prompt submitted to the Bot Group, up to 128 KiB.

ref.description: Ref is the group's public grp_... id or org-unique name from the path.

durationMs.description:
DurationMs is the wall-clock duration of the coordinated execution in
milliseconds.

error.description: Error describes what failed when status is "error".

group.description: Group is the org-unique name of the Bot Group.

groupId.description: GroupID is the grp_... handle of the Bot Group that executed the task.

id.description: ID is the unique grp_run_... identifier for this coordinated execution.

layer.description: Layer is the hierarchy tier at which the group executed.

output.description: Output is the synthesized, consensus-finalized, or leader-approved response.

policy.description: Policy is the coordination policy kind used for this execution.

quasar.description: Quasar carries the Lux Quasar finality certificate when policy is quasar.

status.description:
Status is "ok" when the group produced an answer or "error" when every member
failed.

votes.description: Votes lists each participating member bot's run, proposal, and ballot choice.

runs.description: Runs is the agent's executions, newest first.

points.description:
Points is one bucket per interval across the whole window, in time order and
never sparse: a bucket with no runs is present with v 0, so two lines drawn
from two agents share an x-axis without the client aligning anything. The
window decides the count — 24 hourly for 24H, 7 daily, 30 daily.

v.description: real invocation count in the bucket

budget_micro_usd.description: BudgetMicroUSD is the new cap, or null to remove the cap for good.

id.description: ID is the session, from the path.

budget_micro_usd.description:
BudgetMicroUSD is this session's own ceiling in micro-USD, beyond the agent's.
A replacement must strictly exceed what the session has already consumed, and
removing it is one-way.

budget_removed.description: BudgetRemoved says the session's own cap was taken off. It cannot be put back.

consumed_micro_usd.description:
ConsumedMicroUSD is what has been spent in the current period, in micro-USD.
It is settled from what the gateway reported, not from the quote.

id.description: ID names the session.

status.description: Status is the session's state: running, paused at its cap, or done.

deleted.description: Deleted is true once the session and its events have been removed.

id.description: ID is the removed session's handle.

account.description:
Account is which subscription or API account under that provider served it.
Together with Provider it is what a login revoke matches on to stop the
sessions a withdrawn account was paying for.

actor.description:
Actor is WHO this session belongs to, as "org/sub" — the same identity a run
is billed under. A register that names none takes the calling principal. It is
what scopes a login revoke, so a session with the wrong actor is a session the
right person cannot stop.

agent.description:
Agent is the label the surface running this session calls itself by
("hanzo-dev"), up to 128 characters. Required at register. It is free text,
not a reference: it need not name a defined agent, and nothing resolves it.

base.description:
Base is the branch the run started from. Empty when it took the
repository's default and did not say which.

branch.description:
Branch is the branch the run pushes its work to, and the only one it may
write.

channel.description:
Channel is the collaborative channel this run was started in (HIP-0523), empty
when it came from anywhere else — a CLI, a schedule, an API call. It is what
lets a space view show the runs of one channel beside its messages.

childSessions.description:
Children is the session's DIRECT children, one level down, each with its own
counts. The promoted `children` integer beside it is how many there are; this
is who they are. For the whole subtree, read the tree.

children.description:
Children is the DIRECT fan-out — how many sessions name this one as parent —
and not the size of the subtree. Read the tree for that.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when the row was written, same format. Every path that opens a
session stamps it and StartedAt from one clock reading, so the two are equal
on every session this surface has ever produced.

cwd.description:
Cwd is the directory the session is working in NOW, not the one it started in:
a linked shell moves around, and a card showing where `hanzo link` was run
answers "which work is this" with something that was true once.

endedAt.description:
EndedAt is when its run stopped, same format: it reached done, error or stopped,
or it paused. Empty while it runs; a resume clears it, since it runs again.

environment.description:
Environment is where the run executes: "sandbox" for a Hanzo sandbox, or the
id of the org's machine it was routed to (the same id Target carries).

error.description: Error explains why the session ended in error, when it did. Empty for any other status.

events.description:
Events is how many turns the session's log holds, counted at read time. It is
the whole log, however few of them RecentEvents carries.

host.description:
Execution context (mission-control): the machine/repo/cwd a card shows and
the run-target a session is dispatched to. Omitted when a surface didn't report it.

id.description:
ID is the session's handle, minted here as "sess_" + 32 hex characters. Every
later read, patch, event append and control command is addressed with it, and
a caller cannot choose it.

kind.description:
Kind is what sort of run this session is the view of — "coding" for a coding
run. Empty for a session no run tagged.

lastEvent.description:
LastEvent is the compact latest-activity line for the list projection (nil in
register/patch/tree responses; set by list + detail). It lets a swipe card show
a live one-line preview without fetching full detail.

mode.description:
Mode is what the run may do to its repository: "build" edits, commits and
pushes its branch; "plan" reads and answers with a plan, writing nothing.
Empty for a session no run tagged.

next.description:
Next is the seq cursor to pass as `after` when more events follow a forward
page; omitted on tail reads and when the page reached the end of the log.

org.description:
Org is the caller's OWN tenant, echoed so a client can build the public
build URL (/builds/:org/:project) without a second call or a guess. It is
never another tenant's — every read is org-scoped before it gets here.

parentSessionId.description:
ParentSessionID is the session that spawned this one, making this a subagent
of it. Empty means this session is a root — a flow of its own. A parent always
belongs to the same org, so a tree never crosses a tenant.

park.description:
Park is present while a coding run waits to go on by itself: the model API
refused it for a usage limit, or its payer refused it. The session is paused,
holds no sandbox, and its work is on its branch. Absent for every other session.

pr.description:
PR is the address of the pull request the run proposed. Empty until it
proposes one, and for a run that changed nothing.

progress.description:
Progress is how far along this run is — a share of its goal, a phase, and a
line saying what it is doing. Always present, so a board never branches on
whether it is there; `phase` says "unknown" when nothing has estimated it.
It is a MODEL ESTIMATE wherever `estimated` is true, and the row's own word
where it is false. See progress.go.

project.description:
The readable build: the product this session built and whether its story
is public (provenance.go).

provider.description:
Provider is the linked AI account's provider (claude | codex | hanzo | …) that
served this run. Empty when the surface did not say.

published.description:
Published is the author's decision to let anyone read this session's story at
the public build route. It only ever widens READ access to a session that
already exists and grants nothing else; false, an unpublished session is
invisible there no matter who asks. It cannot be true without a Project,
because that route is keyed on (org, project).

recentEvents.description:
RecentEvents is the page of turns returned for this read, OLDEST of those
first — 50 from the tail by default, up to `limit` (1000 max), or forward
from `after` when paging through the log. The promoted `events` integer says
how many the log holds in total.

repo.description:
Repo is the code the session is working on, as the surface reported it. It is
truth the SURFACE states, so it is a label rather than something resolved here.

rootSessionId.description:
RootSessionID is the top of this session's tree, inherited from the parent and
shared by every node in one flow. A root session's own id, when it has no
parent. It is the key one indexed read pulls a whole flow by, and what ?root=
narrows a list or a stream to.

sandbox.description:
Sandbox is the id of the sandbox the run works in ("m_" and 24 hex), the
handle its terminal and its screen are opened with
(/v1/sandbox/{id}/terminal, /screen). Set when the run leases it, and kept
once the run gives it back, when the id opens nothing. Empty for a run that
never leased one — a routed run, or a turn that only talked.

startedAt.description: StartedAt is when the session opened, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second.

status.description:
Status is one of exactly four: running, paused, done, error. running and
paused are LIVE; done and error are TERMINAL and monotonic — once a session
reaches one it can never go back, because reopening a finished run would
fabricate liveness. A control command never moves it: the surface running the
agent reports the new status, and until it does the command is only recorded.

target.description:
Target is the registered run-target this session is dispatched to — a machine
the org claimed, resolved same-org when it was set, so it can never point at
another tenant's computer. Empty means the session names no machine.

taskRunId.description:
TaskRunID is that workflow's particular run. A workflow is the definition and
a run is one execution of it, which is why both are carried.

taskWorkflowId.description:
TaskWorkflowID is the hanzoai/tasks durable workflow that actually EXECUTES
this session — this registry is the view, control and stream layer over it.
Set, a control command is FORWARDED to that engine; empty, the running surface
polls for commands instead, which is every session today.

terminal.description:
Terminal is where this session can be WATCHED — the URL the machine
published for its live terminal. Omitted when it publishes none.

title.description:
Title is the human line a card shows ("ship the landing page"), up to 512
characters. Free text, and the one field a surface may rewrite as the work
turns out to be something else.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is the session's last-activity clock, same format. It moves on a
write to the row — a status, a title, a re-dispatch — AND on every appended
turn, because the append bumps it in the same transaction. The list is ordered
on CreatedAt, so this is the field that says whether a session is still saying
anything.

next.description: Next is the cursor for the page after this one; empty on the last page.

sessions.description:
Sessions is the matching sessions, each with its event and child counts and
a one-line preview of its latest event.

message.description: Message is the run's own sentence for it, as its thread's card says it.

reason.description:
Reason is "limit" (the model API refused the run's calls for a usage limit),
"payment" (its payer refused them), "fault" (the model API failed them after
the harness tried them again, and the run is tried again by itself) or "restart"
(the pod driving the run was replaced, and it goes on at once on the next).

resumeAt.description:
ResumeAt is when the run is tried again by itself, RFC 3339 in UTC, as the
authority that set the limit states it. Absent when nothing names a time: the
run then goes on when credits are added, a plan or a cap changes, or a person
continues it.

activity.description:
Activity is the one line saying what the run is doing right now ("running
the reaper's tests"), up to 120 characters, in the model's words. Empty
when nothing has estimated it yet.

at.description:
At is when this was determined, RFC 3339 in UTC to the second. Read it as
the estimate's AGE: an estimate is not refreshed while nothing has
happened, and a stale one beside a run that is still moving is itself worth
seeing. Empty when nothing has estimated it yet.

estimated.description:
Estimated says a MODEL produced this, from the run's transcript, and it may
be wrong. False means the session's own row said it: a finished run is 100%
because it finished, not because anything guessed. Never treat a true here
as a measurement — it is the reason to look, not the answer.

pct.description:
Pct is how much of the run is done, 0 to 100. THE KEY IS ABSENT when
progress is indeterminate — a run nobody can estimate is not a run that has
done nothing, and rendering the second for the first is the mistake this
omission exists to make impossible. Read `phase` before reaching for it.

phase.description:
Phase is what shape the run is in: queued, running, blocked, done, error, or
unknown when nothing has estimated it yet. blocked means the transcript
shows the run waiting on something — an approval, a credential, an answer —
which is the one state the running surface cannot report about itself.
error only ever comes from the session's own terminal status. queued is the
run's own word that it is accepted and waiting for a place to start.

account.description:
Account is which subscription or API account under that provider served it.
Together with Provider it is what a login revoke matches on to stop the
sessions a withdrawn account was paying for.

actor.description:
Actor is WHO this session belongs to, as "org/sub" — the same identity a run
is billed under. A register that names none takes the calling principal. It is
what scopes a login revoke, so a session with the wrong actor is a session the
right person cannot stop.

agent.description:
Agent is the label the surface running this session calls itself by
("hanzo-dev"), up to 128 characters. Required at register. It is free text,
not a reference: it need not name a defined agent, and nothing resolves it.

base.description:
Base is the branch the run started from. Empty when it took the
repository's default and did not say which.

branch.description:
Branch is the branch the run pushes its work to, and the only one it may
write.

channel.description:
Channel is the collaborative channel this run was started in (HIP-0523), empty
when it came from anywhere else — a CLI, a schedule, an API call. It is what
lets a space view show the runs of one channel beside its messages.

children.description:
Children is the DIRECT fan-out — how many sessions name this one as parent —
and not the size of the subtree. Read the tree for that.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when the row was written, same format. Every path that opens a
session stamps it and StartedAt from one clock reading, so the two are equal
on every session this surface has ever produced.

cwd.description:
Cwd is the directory the session is working in NOW, not the one it started in:
a linked shell moves around, and a card showing where `hanzo link` was run
answers "which work is this" with something that was true once.

endedAt.description:
EndedAt is when its run stopped, same format: it reached done, error or stopped,
or it paused. Empty while it runs; a resume clears it, since it runs again.

environment.description:
Environment is where the run executes: "sandbox" for a Hanzo sandbox, or the
id of the org's machine it was routed to (the same id Target carries).

error.description: Error explains why the session ended in error, when it did. Empty for any other status.

events.description:
Events is how many turns the session's log holds, counted at read time. It is
the whole log, however few of them RecentEvents carries.

host.description:
Execution context (mission-control): the machine/repo/cwd a card shows and
the run-target a session is dispatched to. Omitted when a surface didn't report it.

id.description:
ID is the session's handle, minted here as "sess_" + 32 hex characters. Every
later read, patch, event append and control command is addressed with it, and
a caller cannot choose it.

kind.description:
Kind is what sort of run this session is the view of — "coding" for a coding
run. Empty for a session no run tagged.

lastEvent.description:
LastEvent is the compact latest-activity line for the list projection (nil in
register/patch/tree responses; set by list + detail). It lets a swipe card show
a live one-line preview without fetching full detail.

mode.description:
Mode is what the run may do to its repository: "build" edits, commits and
pushes its branch; "plan" reads and answers with a plan, writing nothing.
Empty for a session no run tagged.

org.description:
Org is the caller's OWN tenant, echoed so a client can build the public
build URL (/builds/:org/:project) without a second call or a guess. It is
never another tenant's — every read is org-scoped before it gets here.

parentSessionId.description:
ParentSessionID is the session that spawned this one, making this a subagent
of it. Empty means this session is a root — a flow of its own. A parent always
belongs to the same org, so a tree never crosses a tenant.

park.description:
Park is present while a coding run waits to go on by itself: the model API
refused it for a usage limit, or its payer refused it. The session is paused,
holds no sandbox, and its work is on its branch. Absent for every other session.

pr.description:
PR is the address of the pull request the run proposed. Empty until it
proposes one, and for a run that changed nothing.

progress.description:
Progress is how far along this run is — a share of its goal, a phase, and a
line saying what it is doing. Always present, so a board never branches on
whether it is there; `phase` says "unknown" when nothing has estimated it.
It is a MODEL ESTIMATE wherever `estimated` is true, and the row's own word
where it is false. See progress.go.

project.description:
The readable build: the product this session built and whether its story
is public (provenance.go).

provider.description:
Provider is the linked AI account's provider (claude | codex | hanzo | …) that
served this run. Empty when the surface did not say.

already exists and grants nothing else; false, an unpublished session is

by_component.description: ByComponent holds only the components with spend. Absent, not zero.

cap_micro_usd.description:
CapMicroUSD is the total this agent may spend within one Period, as an
integer number of micro-USD (1,000,000 = $1). It is required at creation: a
cap of zero would mean no limit and no per-agent spend record at all.

consumed_micro_usd.description:
ConsumedMicroUSD is what has been spent in the current period, in micro-USD.
It is settled from what the gateway reported, not from the quote.

max_task_micro_usd.description:
MaxTaskMicroUSD is the ceiling for a single run, in micro-USD. A session
cannot exceed it even when the period cap still has room, so one runaway
task cannot consume a month.

period.description: Period is the window the cap resets on: day, week or month.

period_started_at.description: PeriodStartedAt is when the current period began, as a Unix second.

ref.description: Ref names the agent this spend belongs to.

remaining_micro_usd.description: RemainingMicroUSD is what the cap still allows this period, in micro-USD.

failOnce.description: FailOnce optionally names specialist handles whose initial task execution should fail before model invocation, used to exercise and verify selective child-task retry.

lead.description: Lead is the venture lead agent handle or ID; defaults to "venture-lead".

question.description: Question is the research question or brief handed to the venture lead.

specialists.description: Specialists lists the specialist agent handles or IDs to dispatch durable child tasks to; defaults to regulatory-clinical and market-competitive when omitted.

title.description: Title is the headline of the research brief.

venture.description: Venture is the venture slug this brief belongs to.

base.description:
Base is the branch the conversation's coding runs start from, kept as Repo
is. Empty is the repository's default.

developerInstructions.description:
DeveloperInstructions is the explicit alias for Instructions forwarded to
the turn and any coding run it starts; optional.

effort.description:
Effort is how hard a coding run the turn starts thinks: low, medium or high.
Empty is the run's default.

input.description: Input is what the person said, up to 128 KiB.

issue.description:
Issue is the number of the issue on Repo a coding run this turn starts
resolves: its pull request says `Closes #<n>`.

mode.description:
Mode is how the conversation's coding runs go, kept as Repo is: auto starts
them, manual asks the person first, plan reads and answers with a plan,
writing nothing. Empty keeps the conversation's, and a new one is auto.

model.description:
Model is the model the person chose, by the id GET /v1/models lists: the
turn thinks with it, and so does a coding run the turn starts. Empty, or one
the assistant is not offered, is the assistant's own.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository the conversation's code is in, as a coding run names
one: its name in the caller's org, or owner/name on GitHub. Kept for every
later turn; a turn naming another moves the conversation to it, from that
repository's default branch unless the turn names a base too.

session.description:
Session is the conversation to continue: one this op answered with before,
and the caller's own. Empty starts a new conversation.

target.description:
Target is one of the org's machines the conversation's coding runs go to,
kept as Repo is, or `sandbox` for the Hanzo sandbox. Empty keeps the
conversation's, and a new one works in the sandbox.

runId.description: RunID is this turn's run within the conversation.

sessionId.description: SessionID is the conversation: the same id on every turn of it.

deleted.description: Deleted is true when the target was removed.

id.description: ID is the target that was removed.

targets.description:
Targets is every target registered to the caller's org; in a held org, the
caller's own.

capacity.description:
Capacity is a human summary of the machine's size, up to 256 characters. Prose
only; a scheduler reads Spec.

host.description:
Host is the hostname sessions on this machine will report. It is what makes a
re-link IDEMPOTENT: the same (org, host, owner) refreshes the existing row and
answers 200, while a request with no host always creates a new target and
answers 201. It never adopts a row owned by somebody else.

kind.description:
Kind is laptop | cloud | gpu | cluster | machine. Empty registers a `machine`;
anything outside the five is a 400.

label.description:
Label is the name to show for this machine, up to 128 characters. REQUIRED —
it is the only field here a person reads.

metrics.description:
Metrics is a live sample, and sending one IS A HEARTBEAT: it refreshes the row
and starts the 90-second liveness window, and it is appended to the fleet
series as one point. Its own `at` is ignored — the server stamps the time, so
a client can never age or backdate its own machine. Omit it to register a
machine without claiming it is alive.

spec.description:
Spec is the machine's static capability — os, arch, cores, RAM, accelerators.
Every field is bounded on write and at most 32 accelerators are accepted, so
what comes back may be clamped. Omit it for a destination nothing probes.

status.description:
Status is online | offline | draining. Empty registers `online`. It states
INTENT — a heartbeat is what decides whether an online machine is actually
reachable, so declaring online does not make it so.

capacity.description:
Capacity is a human summary of what the machine has ("8 vCPU / 32G", "1× GB10"),
up to 256 characters. Prose for a card — Spec is the same thing in a form a
scheduler can read, and nothing derives one from the other.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when the machine was first registered, RFC 3339 in UTC. A re-link
refreshes the row and leaves this alone, so it dates the machine and not the
connection.

folders.description:
Folders are the folders on this machine the web may start runs in, as its
owner granted them: a run may work in one or under one. A machine reads them
on every heartbeat and drops any folder that is no longer here.

host.description:
Host is the hostname sessions on this machine report, and it is a JOIN KEY, not
a label: a session naming this host counts against the load below even when it
names no target id, and a re-link of the same (org, host, owner) refreshes this
row instead of creating a second. Empty means the machine is addressable only
by ID.

id.description:
ID is the machine's handle, minted as "tgt_" + 32 hex characters. It is what a
session records to say it ran here, and what every later patch, claim or
delete addresses.

kind.description:
Kind is what sort of destination this is, from a closed five: laptop | cloud |
gpu | cluster | machine. A register that named none is a `machine`.

label.description:
Label is the name a person gave the machine ("workshop"), up to 128
characters. Required at register, free text, and the only field here meant for
reading rather than matching.

metrics.description:
Metrics is what the machine was DOING at its last heartbeat — loadavg, memory,
accelerator utilization. Absent when it has never beaten. It is a SNAPSHOT:
the series over time lives in the fleet samples, not here.

metricsAt.description:
MetricsAt is when that heartbeat was recorded, RFC 3339 in UTC, and the SERVER
stamps it — a client cannot backdate or forge the staleness clock. Absent means
never beaten, which is exactly the case where Status is taken at its word.

running.description:
Running is how many of those are in `running` right now — the number a
dispatcher weighs against Capacity. paused sessions are in Sessions and not
here.

serving.description:
Serving says whether a run the caller sends here now would be taken: the
machine is the caller's (or the caller is an org admin), and it is online
with a runner that polled for work within the last 90 seconds — the online
and runner half is what dispatch checks (TargetDispatchable). A heartbeat
alone keeps a machine online, not serving, and a colleague's machine never
serves the caller.

sessions.description:
Sessions is how many of the org's sessions are mapped to this machine, by
target id OR by matching Host. All of them, whatever their status.

spec.description:
Spec is what the machine IS — os, arch, cores, RAM, accelerators — the static
half, changed only when something reports it again. Absent when nothing has
ever been reported, and a scheduler reads absence as "cannot satisfy a floor"
rather than as "no limits".

status.description:
Status is the EFFECTIVE liveness — online | offline | draining — not the
stored one. offline and draining are operator INTENT and are reported as they
stand; `online` is checked against the heartbeat, and a machine that has beaten
before but not in the last 90 seconds reports offline whatever its row says. A
target that has NEVER beaten keeps its stored status, because a hand-registered
destination has no fact to check.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is the last write to the row, same format — which for a beating
machine is its last heartbeat, since a heartbeat IS a write.

children.description:
Children is this node's direct children, each a whole node, so the array nests
to the depth of the flow. A leaf carries null rather than an empty array. The
subtree is materialised in full, up to 10000 nodes, out of one indexed read of
the root; nothing is walked node by node.

session.description:
Session is this node's own session, carrying its event count and its direct
fan-out. It is the same shape the list and detail reads answer with, minus the
last-event preview, which the tree does not fetch.

avatar.description:
Avatar and Emoji re-draw the agent. Sending either replaces the pair, so
setting an image clears a glyph and "" for both goes back to the initial —
there is no state where a row holds two answers.

avatar_licence.description:
AvatarLicence is the licence's short name. Sending avatar or avatar_source
without it clears it, so a replaced image never keeps the old one's licence.

avatar_source.description:
AvatarSource and AvatarLicence say where the avatar image came from. They
move with the image: sending avatar replaces both, so an image sent without
them has none, and sending either replaces the pair.

cap_micro_usd.description: The budget, any part of it. Changing the period opens a new window.

computeRef.description: ComputeRef re-binds (or, with "", unbinds) the visor machine. Opaque here.

description.description: Description replaces the line other agents read in the tool catalogue.

emoji.description:
Emoji re-draws the agent as a glyph. Sending either of the pair replaces
BOTH, so setting a glyph clears an image and "" for both goes back to the
initial — there is no state where a row holds two answers.

executionMode.description:
ExecutionMode switches between one-shot and long-running. The RESULTING
mode+schedule are validated together, so switching to long-running without a
stored or supplied cron is refused rather than accepted into an agent the
scheduler would skip forever. A switch INTO long-running counts against the
per-org cap and can be a 409.

groupId.description:
GroupID assigns this bot to a Bot Group (by grp_... id or name), or removes
it from its group when set to "".

instructions.description:
Instructions replaces the system prompt whole, up to 32 KiB. There is no
append: a prompt is one text, and sending "" clears it.

isPrimary.description:
IsPrimary promotes (with true) or demotes (with false) this bot as the org's
sole Primary Bot; promoting clears isPrimary on every other bot in the org.

layer.description: Layer updates the bot's coordination tier (0..8).

max_task_micro_usd.description:
MaxTaskMicroUSD is the ceiling for a single run, in micro-USD. A session
cannot exceed it even when the period cap still has room, so one runaway
task cannot consume a month.

model.description:
Model re-points the agent at another model, checked against the gateway's
served catalogue exactly as create checks it. Empty STRING is refused — say
nothing to keep the current one. Past runs keep the model that served them.

period.description: Period is the window the cap resets on: day, week or month.

ref.description: Ref is the agent to update — its public id or org-unique name, from the path.

schedule.description:
Schedule replaces the cron. It is validated against the mode this update
leaves behind, and dropped if that mode is one-shot.

serviceAccountId.description:
ServiceAccountID re-points (or, with "", clears) the IAM service account a
scheduled run is billed as. Clearing it puts that spend back on the org.

tools.description:
Tools replaces the whole allow-list, it does not add to it. Sending [] takes
every tool away, which is the only way to say that.

description.description: Description replaces the group's summary when present.

layer.description: Layer moves the group to another coordination tier (1..8) when present.

members.description: Members replaces the group's member bot list when present.

parentGroupId.description:
ParentGroupID re-parents the group (or clears the parent with "") when
present.

policy.description: Policy replaces the group's coordination policy when present.

ref.description: Ref is the group's public grp_... id or org-unique name from the path.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

status.description: The HTTP status.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
